questions.stem: A company runs a fault-tolerant batch image-processing job that can be interrupted and resumed. It wants the lowest possible EC2 compute cost. Which purchasing option fits BEST?

explanation.correct: Spot Instances offer the deepest discount (up to about 90% off On-Demand) for interruptible, fault-tolerant workloads that can tolerate capacity reclamation.

distractors.A: Reserved Instances commit to steady-state usage for 1-3 years; they suit always-on baseline load, not sporadic batch.
distractors.C: On-Demand has no discount and is costlier for interruption-tolerant work.
distractors.D: Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive option, aimed at licensing/compliance needs.

explanation.exam_pattern: Interruptible + fault-tolerant + cheapest = Spot; steady baseline = Reserved/Savings Plans; short-term unpredictable = On-Demand.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Spot)

questions.stem: A production database runs 24/7 at a predictable, steady level for at least the next three years. Which EC2 pricing approach BEST reduces its cost?

options.text: Scaling the instance to zero each night
A Reserved Instance or Savings Plan commitment

explanation.correct: A 1- or 3-year Reserved Instance or Savings Plan gives a significant discount in exchange for a usage commitment, which suits steady, predictable, long-running workloads.

distractors.A: A 24/7 database cannot be scaled to zero nightly.
distractors.B: Spot can be interrupted, which is unacceptable for an always-on production database.
distractors.C: On-Demand is the most expensive choice for steady, predictable usage.

explanation.exam_pattern: Steady, predictable, long-term usage = Reserved Instances / Savings Plans (commitment discount).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Reserved/Savings Plans)

questions.stem: A company wants a commitment-based discount that applies flexibly across EC2 instance families and Regions, and also covers AWS Fargate and Lambda usage, without locking to one instance type. Which option BEST fits?

options.text: Standard Reserved Instances for one instance type

explanation.correct: Compute Savings Plans give a discount for an hourly spend commitment that applies flexibly across EC2 (any family/Region), Fargate, and Lambda.

distractors.B: Capacity Reservations ensure capacity but do not provide a committed-use discount across Fargate/Lambda.
distractors.C: Spot offers discounts but no committed coverage across services and can be interrupted.
distractors.D: Standard RIs lock to attributes like instance family/Region and do not cover Fargate/Lambda.

explanation.exam_pattern: Flexible commitment across EC2/Fargate/Lambda = Compute Savings Plans; max discount, least flexible = Standard RIs.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Savings Plans)

questions.stem: An analysis shows EC2 instances are consistently utilized at only 10-15%. Which action MOST directly reduces cost while maintaining performance?

options.text: Right-size to smaller instance types and use Auto Scaling for peaks
Move the instances to Dedicated Hosts
Buy 3-year Reserved Instances for the current oversized instances
Add more instances of the same size

explanation.correct: Right-sizing to smaller instances matched to real utilization cuts waste, and Auto Scaling handles occasional peaks without permanent over-provisioning.

distractors.B: Dedicated Hosts raise cost and do not fix over-provisioning.
distractors.C: Committing to Reserved pricing on oversized instances locks in the waste.
distractors.D: Adding capacity increases cost without addressing low utilization.

explanation.exam_pattern: Low utilization = right-size (smaller types) + Auto Scaling; don't reserve waste.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (right-sizing)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: EC2 ____ Instances offer the largest discount (up to about 90% off On-Demand) in exchange for the possibility that AWS reclaims the capacity with little notice, making them ideal for interruptible workloads. (one word)

explanation.correct: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at a steep discount and can be reclaimed on short notice, so they fit fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads.
explanation.exam_pattern: Deepest discount + interruptible = Spot Instances.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Spot pricing model)

questions.stem: A company stores objects whose access patterns are unknown and change over time, and wants to minimize storage cost automatically without performance impact or retrieval fees for moving between frequent and infrequent tiers. Which S3 storage class fits BEST?

explanation.correct: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage, optimizing cost with no retrieval fees for those movements.

distractors.B: S3 Standard does not automatically optimize cost for infrequently accessed objects.
distractors.C: Deep Archive is for long-term archival with retrieval latency, unsuitable for unpredictable active access.
distractors.D: One Zone-IA assumes known infrequent access and sacrifices AZ redundancy; it does not auto-tier.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unknown/changing access patterns, auto cost-optimize = S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized storage solutions (Intelligent-Tiering)

questions.stem: Logs in S3 are accessed often for 30 days, rarely after that, and must be archived cheaply for 7 years. Which S3 capability BEST automates moving and expiring this data to cut cost?

options.text: S3 Lifecycle policies that transition objects to Glacier tiers and later expire them
Manually copying objects between buckets each month

explanation.correct: S3 Lifecycle rules automatically transition objects to cheaper classes (e.g., Glacier tiers) as they age and can expire them after a retention period.

distractors.B: Manual copying is error-prone and does not scale.
distractors.C: Disabling versioning does not archive or transition data by age.
distractors.D: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads; it does not tier or expire data.

explanation.exam_pattern: Age-based transition/expiration to cheaper tiers = S3 Lifecycle policies.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized storage solutions (lifecycle policies)

questions.stem: Compliance data must be retained for 10 years, is almost never accessed, and a retrieval time of up to 12 hours is acceptable. Which storage class offers the LOWEST cost?

explanation.correct: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class, designed for long-term archives that are rarely accessed and can tolerate retrieval times measured in hours.

distractors.A: Intelligent-Tiering suits changing access patterns, not decade-long cold data at lowest cost.
distractors.C: Standard-IA costs far more than archival tiers for data almost never read.
distractors.D: Glacier Instant Retrieval costs more than Deep Archive because it offers millisecond access, which is not needed here.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cheapest archive, retrieval in hours acceptable = Glacier Deep Archive; instant archive reads = Glacier Instant Retrieval.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized storage solutions (Glacier tiers)

questions.stem: A team wants to reduce EBS cost on general-purpose SSD volumes while keeping or improving baseline performance. Which change is a straightforward cost optimization?

options.text: Convert all volumes to Provisioned IOPS io2
Increase volume size just to gain IOPS
Move the volumes to instance store

explanation.correct: gp3 generally costs less per GB than gp2 while providing a solid baseline and letting you provision IOPS/throughput independently of size - a common straightforward saving.

distractors.A: io2 is premium-priced for high IOPS/durability, raising cost.
distractors.B: Oversizing to gain IOPS (the gp2 model) wastes capacity; gp3 avoids it.
distractors.D: Instance store is ephemeral and cannot replace persistent EBS.

explanation.exam_pattern: Lower general-purpose EBS cost with equal/better baseline = migrate gp2 -> gp3.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized storage solutions (EBS gp3)

questions.stem: A company keeps data that is accessed about once a month but must be retrieved within milliseconds when needed, and wants lower storage cost than S3 Standard. Which storage class fits BEST?

options.text: An archive-only tier with multi-hour retrieval

explanation.correct: Standard-IA offers millisecond access at a lower per-GB storage price than Standard, suited to data accessed infrequently but needed immediately when requested.

distractors.A: Deep Archive has multi-hour retrieval, which fails the millisecond requirement.
distractors.B: Forcing an archive-only tier adds retrieval latency; IA is the direct fit for infrequent but instant access.
distractors.D: Standard costs more for data accessed only a few times a year.

explanation.exam_pattern: Infrequent access + instant (ms) retrieval + lower cost = S3 Standard-IA (One Zone-IA if single-AZ acceptable).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized storage solutions (Standard-IA)

questions.stem: A finance team wants to be alerted automatically when monthly AWS spending is forecast to exceed a set threshold. Which service BEST provides this?

explanation.correct: AWS Budgets lets you define cost/usage thresholds (including forecasted spend) and sends alerts when actual or projected spending crosses them.

distractors.A: Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities.
distractors.B: CloudTrail logs API activity, not budget thresholds.
distractors.C: Config tracks resource configuration compliance, not spend.

explanation.exam_pattern: Set spend/usage thresholds + alerts = AWS Budgets.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized architectures (AWS Budgets)

questions.stem: An architect needs to visualize and analyze historical cost and usage trends over the past year to find the biggest cost drivers. Which tool is designed for this?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch dashboards for application metrics

explanation.correct: Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes historical cost and usage with filtering and grouping, making it easy to spot the biggest cost drivers and trends.

distractors.B: CloudWatch dashboards show operational/application metrics, not detailed cost breakdowns.
distractors.C: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, not deep cost-trend visualization.
distractors.D: Budgets is for threshold alerts, not rich historical trend analysis.

explanation.exam_pattern: Visualize/analyze historical cost & usage trends = Cost Explorer; threshold alerts = Budgets.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized architectures (Cost Explorer)

questions.stem: A company needs to break down its AWS bill by department and project to charge back costs. Which feature BEST enables this attribution?

explanation.correct: Activated cost allocation tags attach metadata (e.g., department, project) to resources so costs can be grouped and attributed in Cost Explorer and cost/usage reports.

distractors.A: Security groups filter network traffic, not attribute cost.
distractors.B: IAM roles grant permissions, not cost breakdowns.
distractors.D: Placement groups affect instance placement, not billing categorization.

explanation.exam_pattern: Attribute / charge back costs by team/project = cost allocation tags.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized architectures (cost allocation tags)

questions.stem: A company wants automated recommendations that flag idle or underutilized resources (such as idle load balancers or low-utilization EC2 instances) to save money. Which service provides these best-practice checks?

explanation.correct: Trusted Advisor runs best-practice checks, including cost optimization, that flag idle or underutilized resources and other savings opportunities.

distractors.A: Macie classifies sensitive data.
distractors.B: CloudFormation provisions infrastructure as code; it does not flag idle resources for savings.
distractors.C: Step Functions orchestrates workflows.

explanation.exam_pattern: Best-practice checks incl. cost optimization (idle/underused resources) = Trusted Advisor.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized architectures (Trusted Advisor)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: To receive an automated alert when your actual or forecasted AWS costs cross a threshold you define, you create an AWS ______ (the cost-and-usage threshold service).

explanation.correct: AWS Budgets lets you set custom cost or usage thresholds and notifies you when actual or forecasted values exceed them.
explanation.exam_pattern: Threshold-based cost/usage alerts = AWS Budgets (Cost Explorer = analysis/visualization).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized architectures (AWS Budgets)

questions.stem: Instances in private subnets download large volumes of data from Amazon S3 through a NAT gateway, and the NAT data-processing charges are high. Which change BEST reduces this cost?

options.text: Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint so S3 traffic bypasses the NAT gateway
Give each instance a public IP address

explanation.correct: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 routes S3 traffic privately and is free, so it removes the NAT gateway data-processing charges for that traffic.

distractors.B: Transfer Acceleration adds a fee for faster uploads; it does not remove NAT costs for S3 access.
distractors.C: Public IPs route over the internet (still incurring transfer costs) and reduce security.
distractors.D: A second NAT gateway adds cost rather than removing the NAT data-processing charges.

explanation.exam_pattern: Private S3/DynamoDB access without NAT costs = gateway VPC endpoint (free); avoids NAT data-processing charges.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized network architectures (gateway endpoints vs NAT)

questions.stem: A popular website serves the same large static assets to many users directly from S3, and data-transfer-out costs are rising. Which service BEST lowers these costs while improving performance?

options.text: Adding more S3 buckets in the same Region
Moving the assets to S3 Glacier
Amazon CloudFront in front of the S3 origin

explanation.correct: CloudFront caches assets at edge locations, so repeated requests are served from the cache rather than refetched from the origin, reducing origin data-transfer costs and improving latency.

distractors.A: More buckets in the same Region do not reduce data-transfer-out costs.
distractors.B: Glacier is archival and cannot directly serve live website assets with low latency.
distractors.D: Versioning does not reduce transfer costs.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cache popular content at the edge to cut origin data-transfer cost + latency = CloudFront.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized network architectures (CloudFront data transfer)

questions.stem: An architect notices significant data-transfer charges from chatty traffic between two tiers deployed in different Availability Zones. Which approach can reduce these specific charges?

options.text: Keep high-volume communicating components in the same Availability Zone, using private IPs, where resilience requirements allow
Route the traffic through a NAT gateway
Send the traffic over the public internet using Elastic IPs

explanation.correct: Data transfer between AZs in the same Region is billable; co-locating chatty components in a single AZ and using private IPs avoids the cross-AZ charge (balanced against HA needs).

distractors.B: A NAT gateway is for outbound internet access and adds processing charges, not reduce inter-AZ transfer.
distractors.C: Using public endpoints/Elastic IPs can incur more data-transfer cost and reduce security.
distractors.D: Monitoring shows the cost but does not reduce the cross-AZ transfer itself.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cross-AZ data transfer is billable; co-locate chatty components in one AZ with private IPs (within HA limits) to cut it.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized network architectures (cross-AZ data transfer)

questions.stem: A data-processing fleet of EC2 instances repeatedly reads large datasets from S3. To avoid unnecessary data-transfer charges, where should the S3 bucket be located relative to the instances?

options.text: In the same AWS Region as the EC2 instances
In S3 Glacier Deep Archive to lower transfer cost
Accessed only via the public internet
In a different Region to spread load

explanation.correct: Data transfer between S3 and EC2 in the same Region does not incur transfer charges, so co-locating the bucket and instances in one Region avoids unnecessary cost (and latency).

distractors.B: Glacier is archival with retrieval fees/latency; it does not address transfer-cost placement and cannot serve as a live dataset readily.
distractors.C: Forcing public-internet access can add transfer cost and reduce security versus in-Region private access.
distractors.D: Cross-Region transfer between S3 and EC2 incurs charges and adds latency.

explanation.exam_pattern: S3<->EC2 data transfer in the SAME Region is free; cross-Region is billable - co-locate to cut cost.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized network architectures (same-Region data transfer)

questions.stem: A team wants to reduce networking costs for private-subnet workloads that access AWS services. Which TWO actions reduce cost? (Choose two.)

options.text: Co-locate heavily communicating components in the same Availability Zone (within HA limits) to reduce cross-AZ transfer charges
Add redundant NAT gateways in every AZ regardless of need
Use gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB to avoid NAT gateway data-processing charges
Replace all private subnets with public subnets and public IP addresses

explanation.correct: Gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB are free and remove NAT data-processing charges, and co-locating chatty components in one AZ reduces billable cross-AZ transfer.

distractors.B: Adding NAT gateways everywhere increases hourly and data-processing charges.
distractors.D: Exposing workloads publicly reduces security and does not reliably cut transfer cost.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cut network cost = gateway endpoints (free S3/DynamoDB) + keep traffic in-AZ/in-Region + minimize NAT reliance.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized network architectures (endpoints, NAT, data transfer)

questions.stem: A web application's CPU utilization varies throughout the day, and the team wants EC2 capacity to adjust automatically to keep average CPU near 50%. Which EC2 Auto Scaling approach BEST meets this?

options.text: Resizing the instance type by hand each day
A fixed desired capacity with no scaling
A target tracking scaling policy on average CPU utilization

explanation.correct: Target tracking adjusts capacity automatically to hold a chosen metric (e.g., average CPU) at a target value, adding or removing instances as load changes.

distractors.A: Resizing the instance type requires stop/replace and does not continuously track a metric.
distractors.B: A fixed capacity cannot adapt to variable load.
distractors.D: Manual launches cannot react to real-time demand changes.

explanation.exam_pattern: Hold a metric at a target automatically = target tracking scaling policy (dynamic scaling).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (Auto Scaling)

questions.stem: A company wants to run short, event-driven image-processing code that scales automatically from zero to thousands of concurrent executions with no servers to manage, paying only for compute used. Which service fits BEST?

options.text: A fleet of always-on EC2 instances

explanation.correct: Lambda runs event-driven code, scales concurrency automatically, requires no server management, and bills only for execution time.

distractors.A: Direct Connect is a networking service, not compute.
distractors.B: Always-on EC2 means managing servers and paying while idle.
distractors.D: RDS is a managed database, not a runtime for arbitrary application code.

explanation.exam_pattern: Event-driven, auto-scaling, no servers, pay-per-use = AWS Lambda.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (Lambda)

questions.stem: A team runs containerized microservices on Amazon ECS and wants to stop managing and patching the underlying EC2 host instances while still running containers. Which launch option BEST meets this?

options.text: Running containers directly on Lambda layers
Migrating the containers to Amazon S3
The ECS EC2 launch type with self-managed instances

explanation.correct: Fargate runs containers without any EC2 hosts to provision, patch, or scale - AWS manages the underlying compute.

distractors.A: Lambda layers package dependencies; they are not a container host.
distractors.C: S3 is object storage and cannot run containers.
distractors.D: The EC2 launch type still requires you to manage and patch the host instances.

explanation.exam_pattern: Run containers without managing servers = AWS Fargate (serverless for ECS/EKS).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (Fargate)

questions.stem: A tightly coupled high-performance computing job needs the lowest possible network latency and highest throughput between EC2 instances. Which placement strategy BEST supports this?

options.text: A partition placement group across many racks

explanation.correct: A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one AZ for the lowest latency and highest network throughput between nodes - ideal for HPC.

distractors.A: Spreading across Regions maximizes latency, the opposite of the goal.
distractors.B: Partition groups isolate racks for large distributed systems (e.g., Hadoop), not minimal inter-node latency.
distractors.D: A spread placement group separates instances onto distinct hardware to reduce correlated failure, which increases latency.

explanation.exam_pattern: Lowest latency between instances (HPC) = cluster placement group; max fault isolation = spread; big distributed = partition.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (placement groups)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Adding more EC2 instances to handle increased load, rather than increasing the size of a single instance, is called scaling ___ (one word, the opposite of "up").

explanation.correct: Scaling out (horizontal scaling) adds more instances to share load, which also improves fault tolerance; scaling up (vertical) uses a bigger instance.
explanation.exam_pattern: Add instances = scale out (horizontal); bigger instance = scale up (vertical).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (horizontal scaling)

questions.stem: A latency-sensitive production database on EC2 needs very high, consistent IOPS with the highest durability for its block storage. Which EBS volume type BEST fits?

options.text: A general-purpose SSD left at its default baseline
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 / io2 Block Express)

explanation.correct: io2 / io2 Block Express is designed for high, consistent provisioned IOPS with low latency and the highest EBS durability - a fit for critical, latency-sensitive databases.

distractors.A: st1 is HDD optimized for large sequential throughput, not high random IOPS or low latency.
distractors.B: sc1 is the lowest-cost cold HDD for infrequent access, unsuitable for a busy database.
distractors.C: gp3 is SSD, but the scenario calls for the highest, most consistent provisioned IOPS and durability, which io2 targets.

explanation.exam_pattern: Highest/consistent IOPS + critical DB = io2/io2 Block Express; general purpose = gp3; big sequential = st1; cold/cheap = sc1.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (EBS io2)

questions.stem: A big-data workload streams large, sequential reads and writes (log processing and data warehousing) and wants the most cost-effective volume optimized for throughput rather than IOPS. Which EBS volume type fits BEST?

explanation.correct: st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD) is designed for large, sequential throughput workloads such as big data and log processing at a lower cost than SSD.

distractors.A: io2 targets high random IOPS and is far costlier than needed for sequential throughput.
distractors.B: gp3 is general-purpose SSD; st1 is more cost-effective for large sequential throughput.
distractors.C: Instance store is ephemeral and unsuitable for data that must persist.

explanation.exam_pattern: Large sequential throughput, cost-sensitive = st1 (HDD); random IOPS/low latency = SSD (gp3/io2).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (EBS st1)

questions.stem: An application needs the highest possible I/O performance for temporary scratch data (a local cache/buffer) that can be lost when the instance stops. Which storage option offers the best performance for this ephemeral need?

explanation.correct: Instance store is physically attached local NVMe/SSD offering the highest I/O performance for temporary data, accepting that it is lost when the instance stops or terminates.

distractors.A: sc1 is a low-cost cold HDD, the opposite of high performance.
distractors.B: S3 is durable object storage accessed over the network, not the lowest-latency local scratch disk.
distractors.D: Glacier is archival storage with retrieval delays.

explanation.exam_pattern: Highest-performance ephemeral/scratch that can be lost = instance store (local NVMe); persistent block = EBS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (instance store)

questions.stem: A team on gp2 volumes finds that to get more IOPS they must over-provision volume size. They want to raise IOPS and throughput independently of capacity. Which EBS volume type enables this?

explanation.correct: gp3 provides a fixed baseline of performance and lets you provision IOPS and throughput independently of volume size, avoiding gp2's size-to-IOPS coupling.

distractors.B: sc1 is a cold HDD for infrequent access, not independently provisioned SSD IOPS.
distractors.C: With gp2, IOPS scale with volume size, which is exactly the limitation described.
distractors.D: st1 is a throughput HDD, not an SSD with independently provisioned IOPS.

explanation.exam_pattern: gp3 decouples IOPS/throughput from size; gp2 ties IOPS to size.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (EBS gp3)

questions.stem: Users around the world upload large files to an S3 bucket in a single Region and experience slow transfers over long distances. Which feature speeds these uploads by routing through the nearest edge location?

explanation.correct: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest CloudFront edge location and over the AWS backbone, speeding long-distance transfers to the bucket.

distractors.A: Versioning retains object versions; it does not accelerate transfers.
distractors.B: Durability is not adjustable and would not affect upload speed.
distractors.C: Object Lock enforces WORM retention, unrelated to speed.

explanation.exam_pattern: Faster long-distance uploads to S3 via the edge network = S3 Transfer Acceleration.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (Transfer Acceleration)

questions.stem: A read-heavy application on Amazon DynamoDB needs microsecond read latency for repeated reads without changing its DynamoDB API calls. Which solution BEST provides this?

explanation.correct: DAX is an in-memory cache purpose-built for DynamoDB that delivers microsecond read latency and is API-compatible, so the application code needs no changes.

distractors.A: Read replicas apply to RDS/Aurora relational databases, not DynamoDB.
distractors.B: Larger items do not reduce read latency and increase cost.
distractors.D: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not a low-latency cache for DynamoDB.

explanation.exam_pattern: Microsecond caching for read-heavy DynamoDB = DAX (in-memory, DynamoDB-API compatible).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (DynamoDB DAX)

questions.stem: A relational database is strained by repeated identical read queries for popular items. The team wants to cache results in memory to reduce database load and latency. Which service BEST fits?

explanation.correct: ElastiCache provides an in-memory cache (Redis or Memcached) in front of the database to serve hot reads with low latency and offload the backend.

distractors.A: Athena queries data in S3 with SQL; it is not an in-memory cache fronting a database.
distractors.C: Glue is a managed ETL service, not a cache.
distractors.D: QuickSight is BI visualization, not a cache.

explanation.exam_pattern: In-memory cache to offload a database and cut latency = Amazon ElastiCache.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (ElastiCache)

questions.stem: An application needs an in-memory data store that supports replication, high availability with failover, persistence, and advanced data structures (sorted sets, pub/sub). Which ElastiCache engine BEST fits?

explanation.correct: Redis supports replication, Multi-AZ failover, persistence, and rich data structures (sorted sets, pub/sub), which Memcached does not.

distractors.A: Neptune is a graph database, not an in-memory cache.
distractors.B: RDS MySQL is a disk-based relational database, not an in-memory store.
distractors.C: Memcached is a simple, multi-threaded cache without persistence, replication, or advanced data structures.

explanation.exam_pattern: Need replication/HA/persistence/advanced structures = Redis; simple multi-threaded cache = Memcached.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (Redis vs Memcached)

questions.stem: A company wants a MySQL-compatible managed relational database with much higher performance than standard RDS MySQL, storage that scales automatically, and up to 15 low-latency read replicas. Which service fits BEST?

explanation.correct: Aurora is a MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible managed database with high performance, auto-scaling shared storage, and up to 15 low-latency read replicas.

distractors.A: Redshift is an analytics data warehouse, not an OLTP MySQL-compatible database.
distractors.B: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store, not MySQL-compatible relational.
distractors.D: Self-managed MySQL on EC2 shifts all administration to you and lacks Aurora's managed scaling and replica design.

explanation.exam_pattern: High-performance, MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible managed relational with auto-scaling storage + many replicas = Aurora.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (Aurora)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: To scale read throughput of an Amazon RDS or Aurora database, you add one or more read ________ (one word), which serve read-only queries separately from the primary.

explanation.correct: Read replicas serve read-only traffic (asynchronously replicated), letting you scale reads horizontally and relieve the primary instance.
explanation.exam_pattern: Scale reads = read replicas (read-only); HA/failover = Multi-AZ.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (read replicas)

questions.stem: A media company serves images and video to a global audience from an S3 origin and wants to reduce latency by caching content at locations close to users. Which service BEST provides this?

explanation.correct: CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content at edge locations near users, cutting latency and offloading the origin.

distractors.A: Route 53 resolves DNS; it does not cache content at the edge.
distractors.C: S3 buckets have no fixed size, and adding capacity does not reduce global latency.
distractors.D: Direct Connect is a private link from on-premises to AWS, not a global content cache.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cache/deliver content near users globally = CloudFront (CDN, edge caching).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (CloudFront)

questions.stem: A global, latency-sensitive application uses a non-HTTP TCP/UDP protocol and needs two static anycast IP addresses plus fast regional failover, routing user traffic over the AWS global network. Which service BEST meets this?

options.text: An internet-facing Application Load Balancer only

explanation.correct: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IPs, routes traffic over the AWS backbone to the optimal healthy endpoint, and supports TCP/UDP with fast failover - ideal for non-HTTP apps.

distractors.A: CloudFront is optimized for cacheable HTTP(S) content, not arbitrary TCP/UDP with static anycast IPs.
distractors.C: An ALB is regional and layer-7 HTTP; it does not provide global anycast IPs or cross-Region routing.
distractors.D: Route 53 weighted routing uses DNS and is subject to caching/TTLs, so failover is slower than Global Accelerator's.

explanation.exam_pattern: Global TCP/UDP, static anycast IPs, fast failover over AWS backbone = Global Accelerator; cacheable HTTP = CloudFront.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (Global Accelerator)

questions.stem: An application requires very high network throughput and packets-per-second with consistently low latency between EC2 instances. Which capability should the architect use?

options.text: A NAT gateway in front of the instances
Enhanced networking with the Elastic Network Adapter (ENA)

explanation.correct: Enhanced networking (ENA, and EFA for HPC) gives higher packets-per-second, higher throughput, and lower, more consistent latency between instances.

distractors.A: A NAT gateway provides outbound internet for private subnets; it does not boost inter-instance throughput and adds a hop.
distractors.B: Transfer Acceleration speeds S3 uploads over the internet, not inter-instance networking.
distractors.C: EBS size affects storage, not network performance.

explanation.exam_pattern: High pps/throughput, low latency on EC2 = enhanced networking (ENA; EFA for tightly coupled HPC).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (enhanced networking)

questions.stem: A company needs a dedicated, consistent, high-bandwidth private network connection between its on-premises data center and AWS, avoiding the variability of the public internet. Which service BEST meets this?

options.text: A Site-to-Site VPN over the public internet

explanation.correct: Direct Connect is a dedicated private connection between on-premises and AWS, offering more consistent bandwidth and latency than the public internet.

distractors.A: A VPC endpoint provides private access to AWS services from within a VPC, not a link from on-premises.
distractors.B: A VPN traverses the public internet with more variable latency/throughput than a dedicated link.
distractors.D: CloudFront is a CDN, not a private on-premises connection.

explanation.exam_pattern: Dedicated, consistent, private on-prem<->AWS bandwidth = Direct Connect; encrypted-over-internet/quick = Site-to-Site VPN.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (Direct Connect)

questions.stem: A globally used, read-heavy application must reduce latency for users far from the single Region where it runs. Which TWO approaches BEST improve read performance for distant users? (Choose two.)

options.text: Remove all caching so requests always read from the origin
Serve static content through Amazon CloudFront edge locations
Downgrade the database to a smaller instance to save money
Add cross-Region read replicas (or a global database) closer to users

explanation.correct: Caching at CloudFront edge locations and placing read replicas/global database copies closer to users both cut read latency for distant users.

distractors.A: Removing caching increases origin load and latency - the opposite of the goal.
distractors.C: A smaller database reduces performance and worsens latency under load.

explanation.exam_pattern: Reduce global read latency = edge caching (CloudFront) + read replicas/global tables near users.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (global read performance)

questions.stem: A web tier receives bursts of orders that a slower processing tier cannot always keep up with, causing dropped requests. Which service BEST decouples the tiers and buffers requests so none are lost during spikes?

options.text: An Application Load Balancer between the two tiers
An Amazon SQS queue between the web tier and the processing tier
A larger EC2 instance for the processing tier

explanation.correct: An SQS queue absorbs bursts by durably buffering messages until the consumer can process them, decoupling producer and consumer so spikes do not drop work.

distractors.A: An ALB distributes synchronous requests but does not persist messages when consumers fall behind.
distractors.B: Route 53 provides DNS routing, not request buffering.
distractors.D: A bigger consumer still risks drops during spikes and does not decouple the tiers.

explanation.exam_pattern: Buffer bursts + decouple producer/consumer = Amazon SQS (asynchronous queue).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (SQS)

questions.stem: When a new image is uploaded, a company must notify several independent systems at once (a thumbnail generator, an indexer, and an audit logger), each processing the event on its own. Which design BEST implements this fan-out?

options.text: Write the event to a single SQS queue that all systems share and compete for
Store the event in S3 and have each system poll the bucket on a timer
Send the event to one system that then calls the others synchronously
Publish the event to an Amazon SNS topic with multiple subscribers (e.g., SQS queues or Lambda), one per system

explanation.correct: An SNS topic delivers each published message to all subscribers, so every system receives its own copy - the classic fan-out pattern (often SNS to multiple SQS queues).

distractors.A: With one shared queue, consumers compete and each message is processed once, not by all three systems.
distractors.B: Polling S3 on a timer is inefficient and is not event-driven fan-out.
distractors.C: Chaining synchronous calls couples the systems and fails if one is down.

explanation.exam_pattern: One event -> many independent consumers = SNS fan-out (commonly SNS -> multiple SQS queues).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (SNS fan-out)

questions.stem: A company wants to route events from many AWS services and third-party SaaS applications to different targets based on content-matching rules, using a serverless event bus. Which service is designed for this?

explanation.correct: EventBridge is a serverless event bus with content-based routing rules and native integrations for AWS services and SaaS partner event sources.

distractors.A: SQS is a point-to-point queue without content-based routing rules or SaaS event buses.
distractors.B: Kinesis handles high-volume streaming/ordered records, not rule-based routing across SaaS partners.
distractors.C: Direct Connect is a dedicated network link, unrelated to event routing.

explanation.exam_pattern: Rule-based event routing across AWS + SaaS sources = EventBridge event bus.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (EventBridge)

questions.stem: An order workflow has several steps that must run in sequence with built-in error handling, retries, and visibility into which step failed. Which service BEST orchestrates this as a managed state machine?

options.text: A single large Lambda function that contains all of the logic

explanation.correct: Step Functions coordinates multi-step workflows as a state machine with built-in retries, error handling, branching, and visibility into each step's state.

distractors.A: SNS is pub/sub notification, not workflow orchestration.
distractors.C: Packing all steps into one function loses per-step retry/visibility and risks timeouts.
distractors.D: A FIFO queue orders messages but does not orchestrate multi-step workflows with branching/retries.

explanation.exam_pattern: Coordinate a multi-step workflow with retries/state/visibility = Step Functions.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (Step Functions)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: To guarantee that messages are processed in the exact order they are sent and that duplicates are not introduced, you should use an Amazon SQS ____ queue (four-letter type) instead of a standard queue.

explanation.correct: SQS FIFO (first-in-first-out) queues preserve strict ordering and provide exactly-once processing, unlike standard queues (best-effort ordering, at-least-once delivery).
explanation.exam_pattern: Strict ordering + no duplicates = SQS FIFO; maximum throughput, best-effort order = standard.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (SQS FIFO)

questions.stem: A company needs its RDS database to automatically fail over to a standby in another Availability Zone if the primary fails, with no manual intervention. Which feature provides this?

options.text: An RDS read replica in the same Availability Zone

explanation.correct: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby in another AZ and fails over to it automatically when the primary becomes unavailable.

distractors.A: A bigger instance improves capacity, not AZ-level failover.
distractors.B: A read replica is asynchronous and scales reads; by itself it is not an automatic failover target, and same-AZ gives no AZ redundancy.
distractors.D: Snapshots are backups; they do not provide automatic failover.

explanation.exam_pattern: Automatic cross-AZ DB failover (HA) = RDS Multi-AZ (synchronous standby).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (Multi-AZ)

questions.stem: A reporting workload is overwhelming the primary RDS database with read queries, hurting write performance. Which solution BEST offloads the read traffic?

options.text: Add one or more RDS read replicas and point reporting queries at them
Convert the database to a Multi-AZ deployment

explanation.correct: Read replicas provide additional read-only endpoints, so read-heavy reporting can be directed to them, relieving the primary.

distractors.B: Multi-AZ provides HA/failover; its standby does not serve reads, so it does not offload read traffic.
distractors.C: Snapshots are backups, not a read-serving mechanism.
distractors.D: More storage does not reduce read-query contention.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scale/offload reads = read replicas; HA/failover = Multi-AZ. Know the distinction.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (read replicas)

questions.stem: An architect wants a stateless web tier that automatically replaces failed instances and distributes traffic across multiple Availability Zones. Which combination BEST achieves this?

options.text: One EC2 instance in each AZ, started and stopped manually
A single large EC2 instance with an Elastic IP
Several EC2 instances in one AZ with no load balancer
An EC2 Auto Scaling group spanning multiple AZs behind an Application Load Balancer

explanation.correct: An Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs replaces unhealthy instances automatically, and an ALB spreads traffic and routes only to healthy targets.

distractors.A: Manual management provides no automatic replacement or scaling.
distractors.B: A single instance is a single point of failure regardless of size.
distractors.C: Concentrating in one AZ fails if that AZ has issues, and without an LB there is no traffic distribution.

explanation.exam_pattern: Self-healing, multi-AZ web tier = Auto Scaling group across AZs + ELB health checks.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (Auto Scaling + ELB)

questions.stem: A workload needs a load balancer that handles millions of requests per second at ultra-low latency for a TCP-based (non-HTTP) protocol and must expose a static IP address. Which load balancer type BEST fits?

options.text: Classic Load Balancer for HTTP path-based routing

explanation.correct: The NLB operates at layer 4 (TCP/UDP), handles very high throughput at ultra-low latency, and can expose a static IP per AZ.

distractors.B: GWLB is for inserting third-party virtual appliances (firewalls/IDS) at layer 3, not general TCP load balancing.
distractors.C: The Classic Load Balancer is legacy, and path-based routing is a layer-7/ALB feature, not what this TCP scenario needs.
distractors.D: The ALB is a layer-7 HTTP/HTTPS balancer and does not offer the same raw TCP throughput/static-IP profile.

explanation.exam_pattern: Layer-4 TCP/UDP, static IP, extreme performance = NLB; HTTP path/host routing = ALB; appliance insertion = GWLB.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (ELB types)

questions.stem: A company wants users automatically directed to a standby site in another Region if health checks show the primary site is down. Which Route 53 routing policy implements this active-passive behavior?

options.text: Failover routing policy with health checks
Multivalue answer routing without health checks
Weighted routing policy with equal weights

explanation.correct: Failover routing sends traffic to the primary while it is healthy and automatically shifts to the secondary when health checks mark the primary unhealthy - active-passive DR.

distractors.A: Simple routing returns one record set with no health-based failover.
distractors.C: Multivalue returns multiple healthy records but is not designed for active-passive failover.
distractors.D: Weighted routing splits traffic by proportion; it is not automatic primary/standby failover.

explanation.exam_pattern: Active-passive automatic failover by health = Route 53 failover routing policy.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (Route 53 failover)

questions.stem: A mission-critical application must keep serving users with near-zero downtime and near-zero data loss even if an entire Region fails, and cost is a secondary concern. Which disaster recovery strategy BEST meets this?

options.text: A single-AZ deployment with daily backups

explanation.correct: Multi-site active/active runs full production in more than one Region simultaneously, giving the lowest RTO/RPO (near-zero) at the highest cost.

distractors.A: Pilot light keeps only a minimal core running and must scale up on failover, so RTO is higher than active/active.
distractors.B: A single-AZ deployment is not a cross-Region DR strategy at all.
distractors.D: Backup and restore has the longest RTO/RPO because you rebuild and restore after failure.

explanation.exam_pattern: Lowest RTO/RPO = multi-site active/active; cheapest/slowest = backup & restore (pilot light < warm standby < active/active in cost & speed).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (DR strategies)

questions.stem: A company wants a low-cost DR approach where only a minimal core (such as a replicated database) runs in the recovery Region, and the rest of the environment is provisioned and scaled up only when a disaster is declared. Which strategy is this?

explanation.correct: Pilot light keeps a minimal core (e.g., a replicated database) always running in the recovery Region and provisions/scales the rest only when failover is triggered.

distractors.A: Backup and restore keeps nothing running in the recovery Region; it restores from backups.
distractors.B: Active/active runs full production in both Regions at once - far more than a minimal core.
distractors.C: Warm standby keeps a scaled-down but fully functional copy always running, more than a pilot light's core.

explanation.exam_pattern: Minimal core always on, scale up on failover = pilot light; scaled-down full stack always on = warm standby.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (pilot light vs warm standby)

questions.stem: A business states it can tolerate losing at most 15 minutes of data in a disaster. Which metric does the "15 minutes" describe?

explanation.correct: RPO is the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time - here, 15 minutes - and it drives how often you replicate or back up.

distractors.A: An SLA credit is a billing remedy, not a data-loss target.
distractors.C: RTO is how long you can be down (time to recover), not how much data you can lose.
distractors.D: MTBF measures reliability (time between failures), not tolerable data loss.

explanation.exam_pattern: Tolerable DATA loss = RPO; tolerable DOWNTIME = RTO.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (RTO/RPO)

questions.stem: A company must keep a continuously updated copy of its S3 objects in a second AWS Region for disaster recovery and compliance. Which feature BEST meets this requirement?

options.text: S3 Versioning within the same bucket

explanation.correct: Cross-Region Replication automatically and continuously copies new/updated objects to a bucket in another Region (versioning must be enabled).

distractors.A: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads via edge locations; it does not replicate objects across Regions.
distractors.C: Versioning keeps object versions in the same bucket/Region; it does not place a copy in another Region.
distractors.D: EBS snapshots apply to block volumes, not S3 objects.

explanation.exam_pattern: Continuous cross-Region copy of S3 data = Cross-Region Replication (requires versioning).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (S3 CRR)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The AWS service that provides centralized, policy-based backup management across services such as EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, and EFS is AWS ______.

explanation.correct: AWS Backup centralizes and automates backups across many AWS services using backup plans and policies, with centralized monitoring and retention.
explanation.exam_pattern: Centralized, policy-driven backups across many services = AWS Backup.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (AWS Backup)

questions.stem: An architect needs object storage that automatically stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones and is designed for 99.999999999% (eleven nines) durability. Which option provides this out of the box?

explanation.correct: S3 Standard stores objects redundantly across multiple AZs and is designed for eleven nines of durability with no extra configuration.

distractors.B: An on-premises share is not AWS-managed and carries no such durability design.
distractors.C: Instance store is ephemeral and lost when the instance stops or terminates.
distractors.D: An EBS volume is replicated only within a single AZ and is tied to one instance; it is not eleven-nines multi-AZ object storage.

explanation.exam_pattern: Eleven-nines durable, multi-AZ object storage = Amazon S3.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (S3 durability)

questions.stem: A team must back up an EBS volume so it can be restored later, and also create an identical volume in a different Availability Zone. Which AWS feature supports both?

options.text: Enabling S3 Versioning on the volume

explanation.correct: EBS snapshots are incremental, Region-scoped point-in-time backups stored in S3; a new volume can be created from a snapshot in any AZ in the Region.

distractors.A: Elastic IPs are network addresses, unrelated to volume backup.
distractors.B: Instance store is ephemeral local disk, not a backup mechanism.
distractors.D: Versioning is an S3 feature and does not apply to EBS volumes.

explanation.exam_pattern: Back up / clone an EBS volume (and move it across AZs) = EBS snapshots.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (EBS snapshots)

questions.stem: Several EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones must concurrently read and write to the same Linux file system with elastic capacity. Which storage service BEST fits?

options.text: A single EBS volume attached to one instance

explanation.correct: Amazon EFS is a managed, elastic NFS file system that many instances across AZs can mount and access concurrently.

distractors.A: Glacier Deep Archive is cold archival storage, not a live shared file system.
distractors.B: A standard EBS volume attaches to one instance in one AZ and is not a shared multi-AZ file system.
distractors.C: Instance store is local ephemeral disk, not shared across instances.

explanation.exam_pattern: Shared POSIX file system across many instances/AZs = Amazon EFS; single-instance block = EBS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (EFS)

questions.stem: A company stores easily reproducible, infrequently accessed data and wants to minimize storage cost, accepting that the data lives in only one Availability Zone. Which S3 storage class fits BEST?

explanation.correct: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ at lower cost than multi-AZ IA, which is acceptable when the data is infrequently accessed and easily reproducible if that AZ is lost.

distractors.A: S3 Standard stores across multiple AZs at higher cost than needed for reproducible data.
distractors.B: Standard-IA is also multi-AZ and costs more than One Zone-IA for this use case.
distractors.C: Deep Archive is for long-term archival with retrieval delays, not readily accessed infrequent data.

explanation.exam_pattern: Infrequent access + reproducible + lowest cost, single-AZ acceptable = S3 One Zone-IA.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (S3 storage classes)

questions.stem: An architect is removing single points of failure from a three-tier web application. Which TWO actions improve resilience? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enable Multi-AZ for the relational database
Store session state only in the memory of individual web servers
Run the entire stack on one large EC2 instance to simplify management
Deploy the web/app tier across multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer

explanation.correct: Spreading the compute tier across AZs behind a load balancer and enabling Multi-AZ on the database both remove single points of failure.

distractors.B: Keeping session state in local memory ties users to one server and loses state on failure; externalize it (e.g., DynamoDB/ElastiCache).
distractors.C: A single instance is a single point of failure regardless of size.

explanation.exam_pattern: Remove SPOFs = multi-AZ compute + load balancing + Multi-AZ data tier + externalized session state.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (removing SPOFs)

questions.stem: An IAM user has an identity-based policy that allows s3:DeleteObject, but a separate policy attached to the same user contains an explicit deny for that action on the bucket. What is the effective result when the user calls DeleteObject?

options.text: The request is denied, because an explicit deny always overrides any allow
The request is allowed, because an allow exists somewhere
The result depends on which policy was attached most recently
The request is allowed only if a resource-based policy also allows it

explanation.correct: In IAM evaluation an explicit Deny in any applicable policy always wins over any Allow, regardless of where it appears.

distractors.B: A single allow does not override an explicit deny; deny takes precedence.
distractors.C: Policy evaluation is not order- or recency-based; all policies are evaluated together.
distractors.D: A resource-based allow cannot override an explicit deny in an identity policy.

explanation.exam_pattern: IAM decision logic: explicit Deny > Allow > implicit (default) deny.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (policy evaluation)

questions.stem: A platform team wants to let developers create their own IAM roles for applications, but must guarantee those roles can never grant more than a defined maximum set of permissions. Which IAM feature enforces this ceiling on the created roles?

options.text: A resource-based policy on each application
Adding the developers to an IAM group
An IAM permissions boundary applied to the roles the developers create

explanation.correct: A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions an identity can have; delegating role creation while requiring a boundary caps the effective permissions of any role they create.

distractors.A: Resource-based policies control access to a resource, not the ceiling of a created role.
distractors.B: Group membership grants permissions; it does not cap what newly created roles can grant.
distractors.C: MFA strengthens authentication; it does not bound a role's permissions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Delegate identity/role creation safely with a maximum ceiling = permissions boundary.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (permissions boundaries)

questions.stem: A company must grant a specific other AWS account read access to objects in one S3 bucket, with the least operational overhead and without making the bucket public. Which approach BEST meets this?

options.text: Create a security group that allows the other account
Attach a resource-based bucket policy granting the other account's principal the needed read actions
Enable public read on the bucket and filter by referer
Share the bucket owner's long-term access keys with the other account

explanation.correct: A resource-based S3 bucket policy can directly grant another account's principal access to the bucket, a simple cross-account grant without roles or public exposure.

distractors.A: Security groups filter network traffic to ENIs; they do not grant S3 access.
distractors.C: Public read exposes data to everyone; referer checks are easily spoofed and not a security control.
distractors.D: Sharing long-term keys is insecure and hard to rotate.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cross-account access to an S3 bucket with least overhead = resource-based bucket policy (or a role).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (resource-based policies)

questions.stem: A security team must continuously identify which S3 buckets, IAM roles, and KMS keys are shared with external accounts or the public, so unintended external access can be found and removed. Which service is purpose-built for this?

explanation.correct: IAM Access Analyzer uses automated reasoning to identify resources (S3, IAM roles, KMS keys, and more) that are shared with external principals, surfacing unintended external access.

distractors.A: Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data in S3, not external-access relationships.
distractors.B: Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities, not resource sharing.
distractors.C: GuardDuty detects threats from logs; it does not enumerate externally shared resource policies.

explanation.exam_pattern: Find resources shared externally / validate access = IAM Access Analyzer.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (IAM Access Analyzer)

questions.stem: A third-party SaaS vendor needs to assume a role in your account to manage resources. You must ensure that only that vendor, acting on your behalf, can assume the role, preventing a 'confused deputy' where the vendor is tricked into using your role for another customer. What should the role's trust policy require?

options.text: A shared IAM user access key for the vendor
A public S3 bucket to exchange credentials
An external ID condition agreed with the vendor in the role's trust policy
Making the role assumable by any AWS account

explanation.correct: Requiring a unique external ID (sts:ExternalId) in the cross-account role trust policy defeats the confused-deputy problem, since the vendor must present your specific external ID to assume it.

distractors.A: Long-term access keys are insecure and do not address the confused-deputy scenario.
distractors.B: Exchanging credentials through a public bucket is a severe exposure.
distractors.D: Allowing any account to assume the role is the opposite of restricting access.

explanation.exam_pattern: Third-party cross-account role + confused-deputy protection = external ID in the trust policy.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (external ID / cross-account roles)

questions.stem: A company requires that highly sensitive API actions (such as deleting production resources) can be performed only by users who have authenticated with multi-factor authentication. How can this be enforced in IAM?

options.text: Rotate the users' access keys weekly
Set a strong account password policy
Add an IAM policy condition that requires aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent to be true for those actions
Place the users in a separate VPC

explanation.correct: An IAM policy condition keyed on aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent (true) allows the sensitive actions only when the caller's session was authenticated with MFA.

distractors.A: Key rotation is good hygiene but does not condition access on MFA.
distractors.B: A password policy strengthens passwords but does not require MFA at the time of the action.
distractors.D: VPC placement is network isolation, unrelated to MFA enforcement on API actions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Require MFA for sensitive actions = IAM condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (MFA condition keys)

questions.stem: Which practice reflects AWS best practice for the account root user?

options.text: Share the root credentials with the whole operations team
Use the root user for all daily administration to avoid managing IAM users
Create root access keys and embed them in automation
Enable MFA on the root user, remove its access keys, and use an IAM admin for everyday tasks

explanation.correct: The root user should be locked down: enable MFA, delete any root access keys, and perform everyday work with least-privileged IAM identities, reserving root for the few tasks that require it.

distractors.A: Sharing root credentials broadly removes accountability and increases exposure.
distractors.B: Routine use of root is discouraged because it has unrestricted, unbounded privileges.
distractors.C: Root access keys should not exist; they are a major risk if leaked.

explanation.exam_pattern: Secure root = MFA on, no access keys, use IAM identities for daily work.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (root user protection)

questions.stem: A mobile and web application needs to let end users sign up and sign in, including with social identity providers such as Google and Apple, and receive secure tokens, without the company building its own user directory. Which AWS service BEST provides this customer identity?

options.text: Creating an IAM user for each customer
AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD

explanation.correct: Cognito user pools provide a managed user directory with sign-up/sign-in, social and OIDC/SAML federation, and issue standards-based tokens for application (customer) identity.

distractors.A: IAM Identity Center is for workforce SSO across AWS accounts, not application end-user identity.
distractors.B: IAM users are for AWS access and do not scale to large customer bases.
distractors.C: Directory Service provides managed Active Directory for enterprise/workforce use, not app B2C sign-in.

explanation.exam_pattern: App/customer (B2C) sign-in with social federation = Amazon Cognito user pools.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (Cognito user pools)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The AWS service that issues temporary, limited-privilege security credentials (for example when assuming a role) is AWS ___ (three-letter acronym).

explanation.correct: AWS STS (Security Token Service) issues temporary security credentials used by role assumption and federation, avoiding long-term keys.
explanation.exam_pattern: Temporary credentials / AssumeRole / federation = AWS STS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (STS)

questions.stem: A compliance rule requires that every request to an S3 bucket be made over an encrypted (TLS) connection; plaintext HTTP requests must be rejected. How can this be enforced?

options.text: Enable SSE-KMS default encryption on the bucket
A bucket policy that denies requests when aws:SecureTransport is false
Issue an ACM certificate for the bucket

explanation.correct: A bucket policy with a Deny on the condition aws:SecureTransport = false forces all access to use HTTPS/TLS, rejecting any plaintext request.

distractors.A: Default encryption protects data at rest, not whether the connection in transit uses TLS.
distractors.C: S3 endpoints already support HTTPS; the control needed is the policy condition, not a new certificate.
distractors.D: Versioning preserves object versions; it does not enforce TLS.

explanation.exam_pattern: Force encryption in transit to S3 = bucket policy deny on aws:SecureTransport false.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (encryption in transit)

questions.stem: An application encrypts data in one Region and must be able to decrypt the same data in a second Region after cross-Region replication, without re-encrypting or calling back to the first Region's key. Which KMS capability BEST enables this?

options.text: A single Region-specific customer managed key
An AWS managed key in the first Region only

explanation.correct: Multi-Region KMS keys are replicas that share the same key material and key ID across Regions, so data encrypted in one Region can be decrypted by the replica in another Region.

distractors.A: A normal regional CMK cannot decrypt in another Region; its key material is Region-bound.
distractors.B: SSE-S3 keys are managed per Region by S3 and are not designed for cross-Region decrypt control.
distractors.D: An AWS managed key is single-Region and cannot be replicated for cross-Region decryption.

explanation.exam_pattern: Encrypt in one Region, decrypt in another without re-encrypt = KMS multi-Region keys.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (KMS multi-Region keys)

questions.stem: A regulated customer must manage encryption keys in a dedicated, single-tenant hardware security module that they fully control and that meets FIPS 140-2 Level 3, while still running the HSM in AWS. Which service BEST meets this?

options.text: AWS KMS with an AWS managed key

explanation.correct: CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs that the customer fully controls, for cases where a shared, multi-tenant KMS does not meet the requirement.

distractors.B: Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets; it is not an HSM for key material.
distractors.C: KMS is a multi-tenant managed service; it does not give a dedicated single-tenant HSM you fully control.
distractors.D: Parameter Store holds configuration/secret values, not an HSM.

explanation.exam_pattern: Dedicated single-tenant HSM, full control, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 = AWS CloudHSM; shared managed keys = KMS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (CloudHSM)

questions.stem: A financial firm must store records so that, for a fixed retention period, no one - including administrators - can overwrite or delete them (write once, read many). Which S3 feature enforces this?

options.text: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode

explanation.correct: S3 Object Lock (compliance mode) applies WORM retention so objects cannot be deleted or overwritten by anyone, including the root user, until the retention period expires.

distractors.A: Lifecycle rules delete or transition objects; they do not provide immutability.
distractors.B: A bucket policy can be modified by an administrator, so it is not immutable retention.
distractors.C: Versioning keeps prior versions but does not prevent deletions/overwrites by itself.

explanation.exam_pattern: Immutable WORM retention for compliance = S3 Object Lock (compliance mode).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (S3 Object Lock / WORM)

questions.stem: An application needs to store hierarchical configuration values plus a few encrypted secrets that do NOT require automatic rotation, and the team wants to minimize cost. Which service is the BEST fit?

options.text: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (SecureString parameters)

explanation.correct: Parameter Store stores hierarchical parameters and SecureString (KMS-encrypted) values at low cost (standard parameters are free) and is ideal when built-in automatic rotation is not required.

distractors.A: Secrets Manager adds per-secret cost and automatic rotation that this scenario does not need.
distractors.B: Hard-coding values is insecure and unmanageable.
distractors.C: An unencrypted table does not protect secrets at rest.

explanation.exam_pattern: Config + occasional secrets, no rotation needed, lowest cost = Parameter Store; built-in rotation = Secrets Manager.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (Parameter Store vs Secrets Manager)

questions.stem: A customer wants S3 to encrypt objects at rest using encryption keys that the customer supplies on each request, where AWS performs the encryption/decryption but does not store the key. Which S3 encryption option is this?

explanation.correct: With SSE-C the customer provides the encryption key with each request; S3 performs the encryption/decryption and does not retain the key, so the customer fully controls key storage.

distractors.A: SSE-KMS uses keys stored and managed in AWS KMS, not keys supplied per request by the customer.
distractors.B: Client-side encryption means the client encrypts before upload; it is not S3 performing server-side encryption with a provided key.
distractors.C: SSE-S3 uses keys that S3 fully manages; the customer does not supply them.

explanation.exam_pattern: Customer supplies the key per request, AWS encrypts but does not store it = SSE-C.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (SSE-C)

questions.stem: Internal microservices must present TLS certificates to each other, but the certificates are for private internal domains that are never exposed to the internet. Which service BEST issues and manages these private certificates?

options.text: A public ACM certificate for a public domain
AWS Private Certificate Authority (AWS Private CA)
Manually generated self-signed certificates on every host

explanation.correct: AWS Private CA creates a managed private certificate authority to issue and manage private TLS certificates for internal services, with controlled trust and lifecycle management.

distractors.A: Public ACM certificates are validated against public domains and are for internet-facing endpoints.
distractors.C: Ad hoc self-signed certs are unmanaged and hard to rotate and trust at scale.
distractors.D: KMS manages encryption keys, not X.509 certificate issuance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Issue/manage PRIVATE internal TLS certs = AWS Private CA; public certs for ELB/CloudFront = public ACM.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (ACM Private CA)

questions.stem: A policy requires that the KMS customer managed key used to encrypt a data store be rotated once a year with the least operational effort. Which option meets this?

options.text: Enable automatic annual key rotation on the customer managed key
Rotate the IAM user access keys instead
Manually create a brand-new key every year and re-encrypt all data

explanation.correct: Enabling automatic key rotation on a KMS customer managed key rotates the backing key material on a yearly schedule transparently, with no application changes and minimal effort.

distractors.A: Switching to SSE-S3 removes your control over the key and its rotation policy.
distractors.C: Rotating IAM access keys has nothing to do with the data encryption key.
distractors.D: Manual key creation and re-encryption is high-effort and error-prone compared with built-in rotation.

explanation.exam_pattern: Low-effort yearly KMS key rotation = enable automatic key rotation on the CMK.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (KMS key rotation)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: KMS encrypts large amounts of data efficiently by generating a data ___ that encrypts the data locally and is itself encrypted by the KMS key - a technique called envelope encryption. (one word)

explanation.correct: In envelope encryption, KMS issues a data key to encrypt the plaintext; the data key is then encrypted (wrapped) by the KMS key and stored alongside the ciphertext.
explanation.exam_pattern: Envelope encryption = data key encrypts data; KMS key encrypts the data key.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Determine appropriate data security controls (envelope encryption)

questions.stem: A security team must capture metadata about the IP traffic going to and from the network interfaces in a VPC (source, destination, ports, accept/reject) for troubleshooting and intrusion analysis. Which feature provides this?

explanation.correct: VPC Flow Logs record metadata about IP traffic at the VPC, subnet, or ENI level (including accepted and rejected flows), which supports security analysis and connectivity troubleshooting.

distractors.B: CloudTrail records AWS API calls, not network packet-flow metadata.
distractors.C: GuardDuty consumes logs to produce threat findings; it is not the raw flow-capture mechanism.
distractors.D: S3 access logs record object-level requests to a bucket, not VPC network flows.

explanation.exam_pattern: Capture IP flow metadata in a VPC = VPC Flow Logs (no packet payloads).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (VPC Flow Logs)

questions.stem: An organization needs a managed, stateful network firewall at the VPC perimeter with intrusion prevention signatures and outbound domain filtering that applies across many subnets. Which service BEST meets this?

explanation.correct: AWS Network Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall/IPS for VPC traffic, supporting intrusion-prevention rules and domain-based filtering across a VPC rather than per instance.

distractors.A: WAF inspects layer-7 HTTP(S) for web apps, not general stateful VPC traffic/IPS.
distractors.C: Security groups are stateful allow-only filters at the instance ENI, without IPS or domain filtering.
distractors.D: NACLs are stateless subnet filters by IP/port; they have no IPS or domain filtering.

explanation.exam_pattern: Managed stateful VPC firewall/IPS + domain filtering = AWS Network Firewall.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (AWS Network Firewall)

questions.stem: Instances in a private subnet must initiate outbound connections to the internet to download OS patches, but must NOT be reachable from the internet. Which component BEST provides this?

options.text: A NAT gateway in a public subnet, with a default route from the private subnet to it
An internet gateway with a public IP on each instance

explanation.correct: A NAT gateway lets private-subnet instances make outbound IPv4 connections to the internet while preventing unsolicited inbound connections from reaching them.

distractors.A: An interface endpoint reaches specific AWS services privately, not general internet patch repos.
distractors.B: An egress-only internet gateway provides outbound-only access for IPv6, not IPv4 patch downloads.
distractors.D: Public IPs behind an internet gateway make the instances directly reachable inbound.

explanation.exam_pattern: Outbound-only internet for private IPv4 instances = NAT gateway; IPv6 outbound-only = egress-only IGW.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (NAT gateway)

questions.stem: An application tier must accept traffic only from the web tier, whose instances scale in and out so their IP addresses change constantly. What is the cleanest way to express this rule in a security group?

options.text: Use a network ACL that lists each web instance IP
Reference the web tier's security group as the source in the app tier's inbound rule
Hard-code each current web instance private IP in the app security group
Allow the entire VPC CIDR inbound

explanation.correct: Security groups can reference another security group as a source, so the app tier automatically trusts whatever instances belong to the web tier's group, regardless of changing IPs.

distractors.A: NACLs match CIDRs, not security groups, so they cannot track a dynamic fleet cleanly.
distractors.C: Hard-coded IPs break as instances scale and are replaced.
distractors.D: Allowing the whole VPC CIDR is far broader than required and weakens isolation.

explanation.exam_pattern: Tier-to-tier trust with dynamic IPs = security group referencing another security group.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (security group references)

questions.stem: A company uses an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and wants to ensure traffic through it can reach only a specific set of approved buckets, to help prevent data exfiltration to arbitrary buckets. Which control implements this?

options.text: A VPC endpoint policy attached to the gateway endpoint restricting the allowed resources
A security group on the gateway endpoint
