explanation.correct: An endpoint policy on the gateway endpoint scopes which principals, actions, and buckets the endpoint may access, constraining S3 traffic to approved resources.

distractors.A: A NAT gateway is unrelated to constraining endpoint access and would route over the internet.
distractors.C: Gateway endpoints use endpoint policies and route tables, not security groups (those apply to interface endpoints).
distractors.D: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads; it does not restrict which buckets are reachable.

explanation.exam_pattern: Restrict which resources a VPC endpoint can reach = endpoint policy.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (VPC endpoint policies)

questions.stem: A SaaS provider wants customers in their own VPCs to privately consume the provider's application, without VPC peering, without exposing it to the internet, and scaling to many unrelated customers. Which AWS capability BEST enables this?

options.text: VPC peering between the provider VPC and every customer VPC
AWS PrivateLink: publish an endpoint service (behind an NLB) that consumers reach via interface endpoints
A public Application Load Balancer open to the internet

explanation.correct: PrivateLink lets the provider expose a service (fronted by an NLB) as an endpoint service that each customer privately connects to with an interface endpoint, with no peering or internet exposure.

distractors.A: A NAT gateway provides outbound internet access, not a private service-sharing mechanism.
distractors.B: Peering every customer VPC does not scale, risks CIDR overlaps, and exposes whole networks to each other.
distractors.D: A public ALB exposes the service to the internet, which the requirement forbids.

explanation.exam_pattern: Privately expose YOUR service to many consumer VPCs = AWS PrivateLink (endpoint service + NLB).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (PrivateLink)

questions.stem: An enterprise must connect hundreds of VPCs and its on-premises data center with transitive routing through a central hub, instead of building a full mesh of point-to-point connections. Which service BEST meets this?

options.text: A full mesh of VPC peering connections

explanation.correct: Transit Gateway is a hub-and-spoke router that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks with transitive routing, avoiding the N-squared complexity of peering meshes.

distractors.A: VPC peering is non-transitive and one-to-one, so a large mesh is unmanageable.
distractors.B: Internet gateways provide internet access, not private inter-VPC/on-prem routing.
distractors.C: Global Accelerator improves global application reachability/performance, not inter-VPC routing.

explanation.exam_pattern: Many VPCs + on-prem, transitive, central hub = Transit Gateway; simple one-to-one = VPC peering.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (Transit Gateway vs peering)

questions.stem: After adding an inbound allow rule to a subnet's network ACL, responses from the instances are still being dropped. What is the MOST likely fix?

options.text: Attach the NACL to the instance instead of the subnet
Add an outbound NACL rule allowing the ephemeral port range for return traffic, because NACLs are stateless
Add an inbound deny rule for all other traffic
Nothing is needed, because NACLs are stateful

explanation.correct: NACLs are stateless, so return traffic is not automatically allowed; you must add an outbound rule permitting the ephemeral port range used for responses.

distractors.A: NACLs attach to subnets, not instances (security groups attach to ENIs).
distractors.C: An inbound deny does not address the missing outbound return path.
distractors.D: NACLs are stateless, not stateful, so return traffic needs an explicit rule.

explanation.exam_pattern: NACL (stateless) drops responses -> allow outbound ephemeral ports; SG (stateful) needs no return rule.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (NACL ephemeral ports)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The subnet-level, stateless firewall in a VPC that evaluates numbered rules in order and supports both allow and deny is called a network ___ (three-letter acronym, NACL).

explanation.correct: A network ACL (NACL) is the stateless, subnet-level firewall evaluated by numbered rule order, supporting explicit allow and deny.
explanation.exam_pattern: Subnet-level, stateless, ordered allow/deny = network ACL (NACL).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure access to AWS resources (network ACLs)

questions.stem: A security operations team wants a single place that aggregates and prioritizes findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie across many accounts, and runs automated best-practice/compliance checks (such as CIS). Which service provides this?

explanation.correct: Security Hub aggregates and normalizes findings from multiple AWS security services across accounts and runs automated security standard checks, giving a consolidated posture view.

distractors.A: GuardDuty is one finding source that feeds Security Hub; it does not aggregate other services or run compliance standards.
distractors.C: CloudWatch handles metrics/logs/alarms, not security findings aggregation and standards.
distractors.D: CloudTrail records API activity; it is not a findings aggregator.

explanation.exam_pattern: Central aggregation + compliance standards across security services/accounts = Security Hub.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (Security Hub)

questions.stem: After a GuardDuty finding, analysts need to investigate the root cause by analyzing relationships and behavior over time across VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, and DNS logs using prebuilt visual graphs. Which service is purpose-built for this investigation?

explanation.correct: Amazon Detective automatically builds linked behavior graphs from logs to help analysts investigate and determine the root cause of security findings.

distractors.A: Security Hub aggregates/prioritizes findings but does not provide the deep investigative graph analysis.
distractors.B: Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, not incident investigation.
distractors.D: Macie classifies sensitive data; it is not an investigation tool.

explanation.exam_pattern: Investigate/root-cause a finding with behavior graphs = Amazon Detective.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (Amazon Detective)

questions.stem: A governance team must continuously record the configuration of AWS resources, evaluate them against rules (for example, 'no S3 bucket may be public'), see configuration history, and automatically remediate violations. Which service BEST meets this?

explanation.correct: AWS Config records resource configurations over time, evaluates them against managed/custom rules, and can trigger automatic remediation, providing compliance and change history.

distractors.A: CloudTrail logs who made which API call; it does not track resource configuration state or rules.
distractors.B: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks but not continuous config recording, rules, and remediation.
distractors.D: Inspector assesses software vulnerabilities, not configuration compliance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Record config + evaluate compliance rules + remediate + history = AWS Config.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (AWS Config)

questions.stem: During an audit you must determine exactly which identity made a particular API call, from which IP, and when, across the AWS account. Which service provides this record?

explanation.correct: CloudTrail records account activity as events, capturing the caller identity, source IP, timestamp, and parameters of API calls for audit and forensics.

distractors.A: CloudWatch metrics are numeric telemetry, not an audit trail of API callers.
distractors.B: Config tracks resource configuration state and compliance, not the caller of each API event.
distractors.D: Flow Logs record network flow metadata, not API-call identity.

explanation.exam_pattern: Who-did-what API audit trail = CloudTrail; config state/compliance = Config.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (CloudTrail)

questions.stem: A public login endpoint behind an Application Load Balancer is being hit by an HTTP flood and credential-stuffing attempts from individual IPs sending huge request volumes. Which control BEST mitigates this at layer 7?

options.text: An IAM policy on the load balancer
A network ACL deny for all traffic
An AWS WAF rate-based rule that blocks IPs exceeding a request threshold

explanation.correct: A WAF rate-based rule tracks request rate per IP and automatically blocks sources that exceed a threshold, mitigating HTTP floods and brute-force/credential-stuffing at the application layer.

distractors.A: IAM governs AWS API permissions, not inbound web request rates.
distractors.B: Shield Standard protects against common layer 3/4 DDoS, not layer-7 request-rate abuse.
distractors.C: A blanket NACL deny would block legitimate users too and cannot rate-limit per IP at layer 7.

explanation.exam_pattern: Layer-7 flood / brute force rate limiting = AWS WAF rate-based rule.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (WAF rate-based rules)

questions.stem: A media company is licensed to serve its CloudFront-delivered content only to viewers in specific countries and must block access from all others. Which feature BEST enforces this?

options.text: A security group that lists countries

explanation.correct: CloudFront geo restriction (geoblocking), optionally combined with AWS WAF geo-match rules, allows or blocks viewers based on their country, enforcing licensing boundaries.

distractors.A: Security groups filter by IP/port, not by country, and do not apply to CloudFront viewers.
distractors.B: Route 53 routing resolves DNS; it does not block direct access to content by country.
distractors.C: Versioning manages object versions and is unrelated to geographic access control.

explanation.exam_pattern: Allow/block content by viewer country = CloudFront geo restriction (or WAF geo match).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (CloudFront geo restriction)

questions.stem: A company with many accounts under AWS Organizations must centrally define and enforce WAF rules, Shield protections, and security group policies, and automatically apply them to existing and new resources across all accounts. Which service does this?

options.text: AWS WAF configured separately in each account

explanation.correct: AWS Firewall Manager centrally manages and enforces WAF, Shield Advanced, security group, and Network Firewall policies across accounts in an Organization, including auto-applying to new resources.

distractors.B: A Config aggregator consolidates configuration/compliance data but does not deploy/enforce firewall rules.
distractors.C: Per-account WAF configuration is manual and does not centrally enforce across the Organization.
distractors.D: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities; it does not manage firewall policies.

explanation.exam_pattern: Centrally enforce WAF/Shield/SG/Network Firewall policies org-wide = AWS Firewall Manager.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (Firewall Manager)

questions.stem: A security team must keep operating systems on a large fleet of EC2 instances patched on a schedule and report on patch compliance, with minimal manual effort and no inbound SSH. Which service BEST automates this?

options.text: Logging into each instance over SSH to run updates

explanation.correct: Systems Manager Patch Manager automates patch scanning and installation on a schedule via maintenance windows and reports compliance, using the SSM agent without opening inbound SSH.

distractors.A: Manual SSH patching does not scale and requires inbound access the team wants to avoid.
distractors.C: Inspector identifies vulnerabilities (CVEs) but does not apply OS patches.
distractors.D: Config evaluates configuration compliance; it does not install patches.

explanation.exam_pattern: Automated OS patching + compliance at scale = Systems Manager Patch Manager; find CVEs = Inspector.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (Patch Manager)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Requiring token-backed, session-oriented requests to the EC2 instance metadata service - which helps defend the instance's role credentials against SSRF attacks - is enforced by using Instance Metadata Service version ___ (the number or 'v' form).

explanation.correct: IMDSv2 requires a session token obtained via a PUT request before metadata can be read, which mitigates server-side request forgery attacks that try to steal instance role credentials.
explanation.exam_pattern: Protect instance metadata/role credentials from SSRF = enforce IMDSv2.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 1 - Design secure workloads and applications (IMDSv2)

questions.stem: Messages pulled from an SQS queue are occasionally processed twice because a second consumer picks up a message while the first is still working on it. Which SQS setting should be tuned so an in-flight message is hidden from other consumers while it is being processed?

explanation.correct: The visibility timeout hides a received message from other consumers for a set period; setting it to exceed processing time prevents another consumer from picking up the same message.

distractors.A: Maximum message size limits payload size and is unrelated to duplicate processing.
distractors.C: Retention period controls how long unconsumed messages persist, not in-flight hiding.
distractors.D: Delivery delay postpones first delivery of new messages; it does not hide in-flight ones.

explanation.exam_pattern: Stop other consumers from grabbing an in-flight message = tune the visibility timeout.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (SQS visibility timeout)

questions.stem: A few malformed ('poison') messages repeatedly fail processing and keep returning to an SQS queue, blocking throughput. Which configuration isolates these messages for later inspection without blocking the main queue?

options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue with a maxReceiveCount redrive policy
Delete and recreate the queue daily

explanation.correct: A dead-letter queue with a redrive policy moves a message aside after it has been received more than maxReceiveCount times, isolating poison messages while the main queue keeps flowing.

distractors.B: FIFO changes ordering/dedup semantics but does not isolate repeatedly failing messages.
distractors.C: A longer visibility timeout only delays reprocessing; the poison message still returns.
distractors.D: Recreating the queue loses messages and does not address poison-message handling.

explanation.exam_pattern: Isolate repeatedly failing messages = dead-letter queue (redrive after maxReceiveCount).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (SQS DLQ)

questions.stem: Consumers continuously poll an SQS queue that is frequently empty, generating many empty responses and unnecessary API cost. Which change reduces empty receives and cost?

options.text: Use short polling with more consumers
Enable long polling (set a receive wait time)

explanation.correct: Long polling makes the receive call wait until a message arrives (or the wait time elapses), cutting empty responses and request volume compared with short polling.

distractors.A: Short polling with more consumers increases empty receives and cost, the opposite of the goal.
distractors.B: FIFO affects ordering/deduplication, not polling efficiency.
distractors.C: Message size does not influence empty-receive frequency.

explanation.exam_pattern: Reduce empty receives/polling cost on SQS = enable long polling.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (SQS long polling)

questions.stem: Several systems subscribe to a single SNS topic, but each subscriber should receive only the subset of messages relevant to it (for example, by event type), without creating a separate topic per subscriber. Which SNS feature BEST enables this?

options.text: A FIFO topic for every subscriber

explanation.correct: SNS subscription filter policies let each subscription receive only messages whose attributes match its filter, so one topic can serve many subscribers with tailored subsets.

distractors.A: Retention settings do not control message filtering.
distractors.C: A DLQ captures undeliverable messages; it does not filter which messages a subscriber receives.
distractors.D: Creating topics per subscriber is exactly the overhead the requirement wants to avoid.

explanation.exam_pattern: Deliver message subsets to different subscribers of one topic = SNS filter policies.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (SNS message filtering)

questions.stem: A company is migrating an on-premises application that relies on standard message-broker protocols (JMS, AMQP, MQTT) and wants to move to AWS with minimal code changes to the messaging layer. Which service BEST fits?

explanation.correct: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker (ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ) that supports industry-standard protocols like JMS, AMQP, and MQTT, enabling lift-and-shift of existing broker-based apps.

distractors.A: Kinesis is for high-volume streaming, not standard broker protocol compatibility.
distractors.B: SQS uses its own AWS API, so adopting it would require rewriting the messaging layer.
distractors.C: EventBridge is a serverless event bus, not a drop-in broker for JMS/AMQP/MQTT apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Migrate existing broker apps (JMS/AMQP/MQTT) with minimal change = Amazon MQ; new cloud-native decoupling = SQS/SNS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (Amazon MQ)

questions.stem: An application must ingest a high-volume, ordered stream of events and allow MULTIPLE independent consumers to each read the full stream in order and to replay recent records within a retention window. Which service BEST fits?

explanation.correct: Kinesis Data Streams retains records for a configurable window, preserves order per shard, and lets multiple consumers independently read and replay the same records.

distractors.B: A standard SQS message is deleted once a consumer processes it and cannot be replayed by multiple independent readers.
distractors.C: SNS pushes notifications and does not retain an ordered, replayable record stream.
distractors.D: Amazon MQ is a broker for traditional messaging, not a high-volume replayable stream with multiple independent readers.

explanation.exam_pattern: Ordered, replayable, multi-consumer streaming = Kinesis Data Streams; one-time work queue = SQS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (Kinesis vs SQS)

questions.stem: A team needs to run a Lambda function on a fixed schedule (for example, every day at 02:00) without maintaining a server to trigger it. Which serverless approach BEST achieves this?

options.text: An Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule (or EventBridge Scheduler) that invokes the function
A cron job on a dedicated always-on EC2 instance

explanation.correct: EventBridge scheduled rules (and EventBridge Scheduler) trigger targets such as Lambda on a cron/rate schedule with no servers to manage.

distractors.A: Route 53 health checks monitor endpoint health; they do not schedule function invocations.
distractors.C: An SQS delay queue postpones message delivery but is not a recurring scheduler.
distractors.D: An always-on EC2 cron host is a server to manage and pay for, defeating the serverless goal.

explanation.exam_pattern: Serverless cron to trigger Lambda = EventBridge scheduled rule / Scheduler.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (EventBridge scheduling)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: A ___-letter queue (DLQ) receives messages that a consumer repeatedly fails to process, so they can be examined without blocking the main queue. (one word for the hyphenated term)

explanation.correct: A dead-letter queue stores messages that exceed the maximum receive count, isolating problematic messages for troubleshooting.
explanation.exam_pattern: Repeatedly failing messages are redriven to a dead-letter queue (DLQ).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures (dead-letter queue)

questions.stem: An application's load rises predictably every weekday at 08:00 and drops at 18:00. The team wants capacity in place BEFORE each ramp rather than reacting after CPU climbs. Which Auto Scaling approach BEST fits?

options.text: A fixed desired capacity sized for peak at all times
Only a target tracking policy on CPU
Scheduled scaling actions aligned to the known time pattern

explanation.correct: Scheduled scaling changes capacity at known times, so instances are ready before a predictable ramp instead of lagging behind a reactive metric.

distractors.A: Running peak capacity all day wastes money during off-peak hours.
distractors.B: Pure target tracking reacts after utilization rises, adding lag at the start of a known spike.
distractors.D: Manual changes are error-prone and not timely.

explanation.exam_pattern: Known time-based demand pattern = scheduled scaling (combine with dynamic policies for variance).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (scheduled scaling)

questions.stem: Instances in an Auto Scaling group pass EC2 status checks but their application process sometimes hangs and returns errors through the load balancer. The group keeps the hung instances. What should be changed so the group replaces them?

options.text: Set the Auto Scaling group's health check type to ELB so it uses the load balancer's health checks
Move all instances into one Availability Zone

explanation.correct: Using ELB health checks lets the Auto Scaling group consider an instance unhealthy when it fails the load balancer's application health check, so it is replaced even if EC2 checks pass.

distractors.A: A larger maximum does not cause replacement of unhealthy instances.
distractors.B: Disabling health checks stops replacement of any failed instance.
distractors.D: Collapsing to one AZ reduces resilience and does not detect hung apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Replace app-unhealthy (but EC2-healthy) instances = enable ELB health checks on the ASG.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (ELB health checks)

questions.stem: A single public endpoint must route requests to different backend microservice target groups based on the URL path (/api, /images) and on the Host header, over HTTPS. Which load balancer BEST meets this?

options.text: An Application Load Balancer with listener rules for path- and host-based routing
A separate Classic Load Balancer per microservice

explanation.correct: The ALB operates at layer 7 and supports content-based routing rules (by path and host) to different target groups behind one listener.

distractors.A: An NLB operates at layer 4 and cannot route on HTTP path or Host header.
distractors.C: Route 53 resolves DNS; it does not perform HTTP path/host content routing to target groups.
distractors.D: Multiple Classic Load Balancers add overhead and lack modern rule-based routing.

explanation.exam_pattern: HTTP path/host content routing to target groups = Application Load Balancer.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (ALB routing)

questions.stem: When Auto Scaling removes an instance behind an Application Load Balancer, in-flight user requests are being cut off mid-response. Which setting allows active connections to complete before the instance is removed?

options.text: Deregistration delay (connection draining) on the target group

explanation.correct: Deregistration delay (connection draining) keeps a deregistering target in a draining state so existing requests can finish before the instance is removed.

distractors.A: Cross-zone load balancing evens distribution across AZs; it does not drain connections.
distractors.C: Health check interval controls detection timing, not graceful connection completion.
distractors.D: A bigger instance does not address graceful removal of a draining target.

explanation.exam_pattern: Finish in-flight requests on instance removal = deregistration delay / connection draining.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (deregistration delay)

questions.stem: An architect wants to understand how Amazon Aurora provides high availability within a Region. Which statement BEST describes Aurora's design?

options.text: Aurora replicates storage six ways across three Availability Zones and can automatically fail over to an Aurora Replica
Aurora requires manual data copying to a standby you manage
Aurora keeps all replicas in a single Availability Zone
Aurora stores a single copy of data on one instance's local disk

explanation.correct: Aurora's storage layer keeps multiple copies of data across three AZs and, on a primary failure, promotes an Aurora Replica to minimize downtime without manual data movement.

distractors.B: Aurora replication and failover are managed, not manual copying.
distractors.C: Aurora distributes storage across multiple AZs, not a single AZ.
distractors.D: Aurora does not rely on a single local-disk copy; its storage is distributed and replicated.

explanation.exam_pattern: Aurora HA = distributed multi-AZ storage + automatic promotion of a replica.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (Aurora failover)

questions.stem: A globally used application needs a database with local low-latency reads AND writes in multiple Regions, staying available even if an entire Region fails. Which solution BEST meets this?

options.text: A single-Region DynamoDB table with daily backups
An RDS Multi-AZ deployment in one Region
A DynamoDB table with only a local secondary index

explanation.correct: DynamoDB global tables replicate across chosen Regions with multi-active read/write, giving low-latency local access and resilience to a full Region failure.

distractors.A: A single-Region table with backups cannot serve local writes in other Regions or survive a Region loss without restore.
distractors.C: RDS Multi-AZ provides single-Region HA, not multi-Region active read/write.
distractors.D: A local secondary index changes query options within one table, not multi-Region replication.

explanation.exam_pattern: Multi-Region, multi-active NoSQL with local read/write = DynamoDB global tables.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (DynamoDB global tables)

questions.stem: A caching tier must remain available if a cache node or its Availability Zone fails, automatically promoting a replica with minimal disruption. Which option BEST provides this?

options.text: A single-node ElastiCache for Memcached cluster
ElastiCache for Redis with a Multi-AZ replication group and automatic failover
A standalone Redis node in one AZ

explanation.correct: ElastiCache for Redis supports replication groups across AZs with automatic failover, promoting a replica if the primary or its AZ fails.

distractors.A: DAX is an in-memory cache specifically for DynamoDB, not a general caching tier with this framing.
distractors.B: Memcached does not provide replication or automatic failover.
distractors.D: A single node in one AZ is a single point of failure.

explanation.exam_pattern: Highly available cache with failover = ElastiCache for Redis Multi-AZ replication group.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (ElastiCache Redis Multi-AZ)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: To withstand the failure of a single data center, deploy an Auto Scaling group across multiple ___ ___ within a Region (two words, abbreviated AZs).

explanation.correct: Spreading instances across multiple Availability Zones ensures the workload survives the loss of any single AZ (data center).
explanation.exam_pattern: Survive a data-center failure = spread across multiple Availability Zones.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (multi-AZ)

questions.stem: A company wants a DR approach where a scaled-down but FULLY FUNCTIONAL copy of the production stack runs continuously in a second Region and is scaled up to full capacity on failover, giving a shorter RTO than keeping only a minimal core running. Which strategy is this?

explanation.correct: Warm standby keeps a smaller but fully working replica of the environment always running, which is scaled up on failover - faster RTO than pilot light, cheaper than active/active.

distractors.B: Pilot light keeps only a minimal core (e.g., a database) running, not a fully functional scaled-down stack.
distractors.C: Single-AZ with snapshots is not a cross-Region DR strategy.
distractors.D: Backup and restore keeps nothing running and has the longest RTO.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scaled-down but fully functional always-on standby = warm standby; minimal core = pilot light.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (warm standby)

questions.stem: An Aurora-backed application needs cross-Region disaster recovery with very low replication lag and the ability to promote the secondary Region quickly if the primary Region fails. Which feature is PURPOSE-BUILT for this?

options.text: Daily manual snapshots copied to the second Region
A single standard cross-Region read replica with manual scripts

explanation.correct: Aurora Global Database replicates to secondary Regions with typically low lag and supports fast promotion of a secondary Region, which is designed for cross-Region DR.

distractors.A: Multi-AZ provides single-Region HA, not cross-Region DR.
distractors.B: Daily snapshot copies give a large RPO and slow recovery compared with continuous replication.
distractors.D: A plain cross-Region read replica has higher lag and manual, less integrated failover than Global Database.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cross-Region DR for Aurora with low lag + fast promotion = Aurora Global Database.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (Aurora Global Database)

questions.stem: To defend against ransomware and malicious insiders, a company must ensure backups cannot be deleted or altered before their retention period expires - even by an administrator. Which capability BEST provides this?

options.text: Storing backups on a single EBS volume
AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode
An IAM policy that denies deletes (which an admin can later change)

explanation.correct: AWS Backup Vault Lock (compliance mode) enforces WORM on recovery points so backups cannot be deleted or their retention shortened until expiry, even by privileged users.

distractors.A: A single EBS volume is neither immutable nor resilient.
distractors.C: An IAM deny can be modified or bypassed by someone with sufficient privileges, so it is not immutable.
distractors.D: Backing up more often does not make existing backups immutable.

explanation.exam_pattern: Immutable, un-deletable backups (ransomware defense) = AWS Backup Vault Lock (compliance mode).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (Backup Vault Lock)

questions.stem: A security team wants backups isolated so that even if a workload account is fully compromised, the backups remain intact in a separate account. Which AWS Backup capability BEST supports this?

options.text: Manual snapshots stored on the production instances
Relying only on S3 Cross-Region Replication
Keeping all backups in the same account as the workload
Cross-account backup copy to a dedicated, isolated backup account (via AWS Organizations)

explanation.correct: AWS Backup can copy recovery points to a vault in a separate, centrally managed account, so compromise of the workload account does not reach the isolated backups.

distractors.A: Snapshots on production instances are lost with those instances and are not isolated.
distractors.B: CRR replicates S3 objects across Regions but does not provide account isolation of backups for all services.
distractors.C: Backups in the same account share its blast radius if that account is compromised.

explanation.exam_pattern: Isolate backups from a compromised account = AWS Backup cross-account copy to a separate backup account.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (cross-account backup)

questions.stem: A compliance rule requires that objects written to a production S3 bucket be automatically copied to a separate bucket in the SAME Region (for example, a log-aggregation or audit bucket in another account). Which S3 feature BEST meets this?

explanation.correct: Same-Region Replication automatically copies objects to another bucket in the same Region, which suits log aggregation, compliance, and cross-account copies without changing Region.

distractors.A: Lifecycle transitions change storage class; they do not copy objects to another bucket.
distractors.C: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads from distant clients; it does not replicate objects.
distractors.D: CRR replicates to a different Region, which is not what a same-Region requirement needs.

explanation.exam_pattern: Auto-copy objects to another bucket in the same Region = S3 SRR; different Region = CRR.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (S3 SRR)

questions.stem: A team wants to automate creation, retention, and cross-Region copy of EBS snapshots on a schedule for disaster recovery, without writing custom scripts. Which service BEST provides this?

options.text: Manually taking snapshots when someone remembers

explanation.correct: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager automates EBS snapshot (and AMI) creation, retention, and cross-Region/cross-account copy on a schedule, removing custom scripting.

distractors.A: Transfer Acceleration speeds S3 uploads; it does not manage EBS snapshots.
distractors.C: Instance store is ephemeral and cannot be snapshotted for DR.
distractors.D: Manual snapshots are inconsistent and do not guarantee retention or cross-Region copies.

explanation.exam_pattern: Automate EBS snapshot schedule/retention/cross-Region copy = Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (Data Lifecycle Manager)

questions.stem: After a bad data change, a team needs to restore an Amazon RDS database to the exact state it was in a few minutes before the change, within the backup retention window. Which capability makes this possible?

options.text: A single manual snapshot taken last week

explanation.correct: RDS automated backups (with transaction logs) allow point-in-time recovery to any second within the retention window, so you can restore to just before the bad change.

distractors.B: A read replica serves reads; it does not provide point-in-time restore of prior state.
distractors.C: Multi-AZ provides failover of the current data, not recovery to an earlier point in time.
distractors.D: A weekly manual snapshot only restores to that snapshot time, not to minutes before the incident.

explanation.exam_pattern: Restore to a precise earlier moment = RDS automated backups / point-in-time recovery.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (RDS PITR)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The DR strategy that keeps a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the workload always running in the recovery Region, then scales it up on failover, is called ___ standby. (one word)

explanation.correct: Warm standby keeps a reduced-capacity but functional environment running continuously and scales it to full size during failover.
explanation.exam_pattern: Always-on scaled-down functional standby = warm standby (faster RTO than pilot light).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (warm standby)

questions.stem: A fleet of Windows application servers across two Availability Zones needs a highly available shared file system that uses the SMB protocol and integrates with Active Directory. Which service BEST fits?

options.text: Amazon S3 mounted as a drive
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server (Multi-AZ)

explanation.correct: FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed SMB file shares with Active Directory integration and a Multi-AZ option for high availability.

distractors.A: EFS is an NFS file system for Linux workloads, not native Windows/SMB with AD.
distractors.B: A standard EBS volume attaches to one instance in one AZ and is not a shared, HA SMB share.
distractors.C: S3 is object storage, not an SMB file system for Windows applications.

explanation.exam_pattern: HA shared Windows/SMB file storage with AD = FSx for Windows File Server (Multi-AZ); Linux/NFS = EFS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (FSx for Windows)

questions.stem: A bucket holds critical objects that must be protected against accidental AND malicious permanent deletion, including by a user whose credentials are stolen. Which combination BEST protects the data?

options.text: Rely on a bucket policy alone
Turn off logging to reduce noise
Enable a Lifecycle rule that expires objects after 30 days
Enable S3 Versioning and MFA Delete

explanation.correct: Versioning preserves prior versions so overwrites/deletes are recoverable, and MFA Delete requires an MFA code to permanently delete a version or change versioning state.

distractors.A: A bucket policy can be altered and does not retain prior versions for recovery.
distractors.B: Disabling logging reduces visibility and provides no deletion protection.
distractors.C: A lifecycle expiration rule deletes objects, increasing the risk of data loss, not protecting it.

explanation.exam_pattern: Protect S3 objects from accidental/malicious deletion = Versioning + MFA Delete.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (versioning + MFA Delete)

questions.stem: Amazon S3 Standard is described as providing 99.999999999% (eleven nines) DURABILITY. What does this durability figure primarily describe?

options.text: The number of API calls allowed per second
The percentage of time the service is reachable for requests (its uptime)
The expected probability of NOT losing a stored object over a year, achieved via redundancy across multiple AZs

explanation.correct: Durability measures the likelihood that stored data is not lost over time; S3 achieves it by redundantly storing objects across multiple devices and Availability Zones.

distractors.A: Latency is a performance metric, not durability.
distractors.B: Request rate is a throughput/limit concept, not durability.
distractors.C: That describes availability (uptime), a separate metric from durability.

explanation.exam_pattern: Durability = data not lost over time; availability = able to access it when needed.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (durability vs availability)

questions.stem: A shared file system used by production workloads must continue to operate even if an entire Availability Zone is lost. Which EFS configuration BEST meets this resilience requirement?

options.text: EFS Standard storage classes, which store data redundantly across multiple AZs in the Region
A single EBS volume in one AZ

explanation.correct: EFS Standard (regional) storage classes store data across multiple AZs, so the file system remains available if a single AZ fails.

distractors.A: EFS One Zone stores data in a single AZ at lower cost and does not survive that AZ's loss.
distractors.B: Instance store is ephemeral local disk, not resilient shared storage.
distractors.D: An EBS volume lives in one AZ and is not a multi-AZ shared file system.

explanation.exam_pattern: Survive an AZ failure for shared files = EFS Standard (regional/multi-AZ); cheaper single-AZ = EFS One Zone.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (EFS Standard vs One Zone)

questions.stem: A team discovered that important data written to an EC2 instance store volume was lost after the instance was stopped. Which design change prevents this in the future?

options.text: Take no action; instance store is durable
Enable S3 Versioning on the instance store
Use a larger instance store volume
Store the persistent data on an EBS volume (or EFS/S3), not on instance store

explanation.correct: Instance store is ephemeral and is lost when an instance stops/terminates; persistent data belongs on EBS, EFS, or S3, which survive the instance lifecycle.

distractors.A: Instance store is not durable; the premise is incorrect.
distractors.B: Versioning is an S3 feature and cannot be applied to instance store.
distractors.C: A larger instance store is still ephemeral and will still be lost on stop.

explanation.exam_pattern: Persistent data must not live on instance store (ephemeral); use EBS/EFS/S3.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (instance store volatility)

questions.stem: An architect wants EBS-backed data to be resilient to both Availability Zone and Region-level events. Which TWO actions BEST support this? (Choose two.)

options.text: Place the single volume in one Availability Zone with no backups
Keep the only copy of the data on instance store
Take regular EBS snapshots (stored durably and restorable to any AZ in the Region)
Copy EBS snapshots to a second Region for disaster recovery

explanation.correct: Regular snapshots let you recreate volumes in any AZ, and copying snapshots to another Region provides recovery if the primary Region is impaired.

distractors.A: A single unbacked volume in one AZ is a single point of failure.
distractors.B: Instance store is ephemeral and offers no resilience.

explanation.exam_pattern: Resilient EBS data = regular snapshots (any-AZ restore) + cross-Region snapshot copies for DR.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (EBS snapshot resilience)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Enabling S3 ___ keeps multiple variants of an object in the same bucket, so you can recover from accidental overwrites or deletes. (one word)

explanation.correct: S3 Versioning preserves previous object versions, allowing recovery from unintended overwrites or deletions.
explanation.exam_pattern: Recover from overwrite/delete in S3 = enable Versioning (pair with MFA Delete for stronger protection).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 2 - Design highly available / fault-tolerant architectures (S3 Versioning)

questions.stem: A latency-sensitive API runs on AWS Lambda, but users experience slow responses when traffic spikes because new execution environments must initialize (cold starts). Which Lambda feature BEST reduces this cold-start latency?

explanation.correct: Provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of execution environments initialized and ready, eliminating cold-start latency for predictable or latency-sensitive traffic.

distractors.A: A larger package can worsen, not reduce, cold-start time.
distractors.C: A longer timeout allows longer runs; it does not remove initialization latency.
distractors.D: Reserved concurrency caps/guarantees the number of concurrent executions but does not pre-warm environments.

explanation.exam_pattern: Kill Lambda cold-start latency = provisioned concurrency; cap concurrency = reserved concurrency.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (provisioned concurrency)

questions.stem: A Lambda function connects to a small downstream database that can handle only a limited number of concurrent connections. During spikes, Lambda scales up and overwhelms the database. Which Lambda setting BEST limits this?

options.text: Set reserved concurrency to cap the function's maximum concurrent executions
Enable provisioned concurrency with a high value

explanation.correct: Reserved concurrency sets a ceiling on how many instances of the function can run at once, protecting a connection-limited downstream resource from being overwhelmed.

distractors.A: More memory speeds execution; it does not limit concurrency.
distractors.C: Provisioned concurrency pre-warms environments but, if high, would still allow many concurrent connections.
distractors.D: A longer timeout does not cap concurrent executions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Protect a limited downstream from Lambda scaling = reserved concurrency (concurrency cap).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (reserved concurrency)

questions.stem: A workload runs a large in-memory analytics database that needs a very high ratio of RAM to vCPU. Which EC2 instance category is the BEST starting point?

options.text: Memory-optimized instances (for example, the R family)

explanation.correct: Memory-optimized instances provide a high amount of RAM per vCPU, matching in-memory databases and large caches.

distractors.A: Burstable general-purpose instances are for small, bursty workloads, not large in-memory databases.
distractors.B: Storage-optimized instances target high local I/O, not maximal RAM.
distractors.D: Compute-optimized instances favor high CPU per memory, better for compute-bound workloads.

explanation.exam_pattern: Match the instance family to the bottleneck: memory-heavy = R; CPU-heavy = C; local I/O = I/D; bursty = T.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (instance families)

questions.stem: An Auto Scaling group runs an application whose instances take several minutes to boot and warm up, which delays scale-out during sudden demand. Which feature pre-initializes instances so they can be added to service quickly?

explanation.correct: Warm pools maintain pre-initialized (stopped or running) instances that can be brought into service rapidly, reducing scale-out latency for slow-booting applications.

distractors.A: Provisioned concurrency is a Lambda feature, not applicable to EC2 Auto Scaling.
distractors.B: A spread placement group affects hardware isolation, not boot/warm-up time.
distractors.C: A larger volume does not shorten application warm-up.

explanation.exam_pattern: Slow-booting app + faster scale-out = Auto Scaling warm pools.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (warm pools)

questions.stem: A team has standardized on Kubernetes and wants AWS to run and manage the Kubernetes control plane while they deploy their existing Kubernetes manifests. Which service BEST fits?

options.text: Plain EC2 instances managed by hand
Amazon ECS with the AWS-proprietary task model

explanation.correct: Amazon EKS provides a managed Kubernetes control plane, letting teams run standard Kubernetes workloads without operating the control plane themselves.

distractors.A: Self-managed EC2 means building and operating Kubernetes yourself.
distractors.B: Lambda is function-based serverless, not a Kubernetes platform.
distractors.C: ECS is AWS's own orchestration model, not upstream Kubernetes-compatible.

explanation.exam_pattern: Managed upstream Kubernetes = Amazon EKS; AWS-native container orchestration = ECS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (EKS)

questions.stem: A tightly coupled HPC simulation uses MPI and needs the lowest possible inter-node latency with OS-bypass networking to scale across many EC2 instances. Which networking capability BEST supports this?

options.text: A larger EBS volume with more IOPS
An Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) attached to the instances

explanation.correct: EFA provides OS-bypass, low-latency, high-throughput networking for tightly coupled HPC/MPI workloads, enabling them to scale efficiently across instances (usually in a cluster placement group).

distractors.A: A NAT gateway is for outbound internet access and adds latency, not HPC networking.
distractors.B: Transfer Acceleration speeds S3 uploads over the internet, unrelated to inter-node HPC traffic.
distractors.C: More EBS IOPS improves storage I/O, not inter-node network latency.

explanation.exam_pattern: Tightly coupled HPC/MPI with OS-bypass low latency = Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (EFA)

questions.stem: An architect wants Auto Scaling to add a DIFFERENT number of instances depending on HOW FAR a metric exceeds its threshold (a small breach adds a few, a large breach adds many). Which scaling policy type BEST supports this?

explanation.correct: Step scaling defines multiple steps that apply different capacity adjustments based on the magnitude of the alarm breach, responding proportionally to demand.

distractors.A: Simple scaling applies a single adjustment and waits for a cooldown before acting again.
distractors.C: Scheduled scaling changes capacity at set times, not by breach magnitude.
distractors.D: Manual scaling requires human action and cannot respond proportionally in real time.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scale by breach magnitude = step scaling; single fixed change = simple scaling; known times = scheduled.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (step scaling)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: To eliminate cold-start latency for a latency-sensitive Lambda function by keeping execution environments initialized and ready, enable ___ concurrency. (one word)

explanation.correct: Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes a specified number of Lambda execution environments so invocations avoid cold starts.
explanation.exam_pattern: Pre-warmed Lambda = provisioned concurrency; cap concurrent runs = reserved concurrency.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions (provisioned concurrency)

questions.stem: An application must sustain a very high rate of S3 GET and PUT requests. Which approach BEST increases achievable request throughput on the bucket?

options.text: Spread objects across many key prefixes so requests parallelize across S3 partitions
Enable S3 Versioning to add throughput
Store all objects under a single identical prefix

explanation.correct: S3 scales request rate per prefix, so distributing objects across multiple prefixes lets requests parallelize and achieve higher aggregate throughput.

distractors.B: Versioning manages object versions; it does not raise request throughput.
distractors.C: Durability is not adjustable and is unrelated to request throughput.
distractors.D: Concentrating everything under one prefix limits how requests parallelize.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scale S3 request rate = parallelize across multiple key prefixes.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (S3 prefixes)

questions.stem: A client must upload multi-gigabyte objects to S3 as fast and reliably as possible, with the ability to retry only the failed portions instead of restarting the whole upload. Which approach BEST meets this?

options.text: Multipart upload (upload parts in parallel; retry individual parts)
Store the file on instance store instead
A single PUT of the entire object

explanation.correct: Multipart upload splits a large object into parts uploaded in parallel; failed parts can be retried individually, improving speed and resilience for large objects.

distractors.A: Versioning does not accelerate or make large uploads resumable.
distractors.C: Instance store is ephemeral local disk, not an S3 upload method.
distractors.D: A single large PUT cannot parallelize and must restart entirely on failure.

explanation.exam_pattern: Large object upload, parallel + resumable parts = S3 multipart upload.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (multipart upload)

questions.stem: A high-performance computing and machine-learning workload needs a shared file system delivering very high throughput and sub-millisecond latency, and it must process large datasets that live in Amazon S3. Which service BEST fits?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Lustre (linked to the S3 data)

explanation.correct: FSx for Lustre is a high-performance parallel file system built for HPC/ML, offering very high throughput and low latency and integrating directly with S3 datasets.

distractors.A: Glacier is archival storage with retrieval delays, not a live high-performance file system.
distractors.B: A single gp2 volume attaches to one instance and cannot provide a shared HPC-scale file system.
distractors.D: EFS is a general-purpose NFS file system and does not match Lustre's HPC throughput/latency profile.

explanation.exam_pattern: HPC/ML high-throughput shared file system tied to S3 = FSx for Lustre.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (FSx for Lustre)

questions.stem: A clustered application needs a SINGLE block volume that multiple EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone can attach and write to concurrently, coordinated by a cluster-aware file system. Which capability enables this?

options.text: Amazon EFS mounted on each instance
Attaching a gp3 volume to many instances at once
EC2 instance store shared between instances
EBS Multi-Attach on a Provisioned IOPS (io2) volume

explanation.correct: EBS Multi-Attach lets a single io1/io2 Provisioned IOPS volume attach to multiple instances in the same AZ for concurrent block access, requiring a cluster-aware file system to coordinate writes.

distractors.A: EFS is a shared FILE system (NFS), not a single shared BLOCK volume.
distractors.B: gp3 does not support Multi-Attach; Multi-Attach is limited to io1/io2.
distractors.C: Instance store is local, ephemeral, and cannot be shared across instances.

explanation.exam_pattern: One block volume shared by multiple instances in an AZ = EBS Multi-Attach (io1/io2, cluster-aware FS); shared files = EFS.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (EBS Multi-Attach)

questions.stem: An EFS file system serves a workload whose throughput demand is spiky and unpredictable, and the team wants throughput to scale automatically without paying for fixed provisioned throughput during idle periods. Which EFS throughput mode BEST fits?

options.text: Bursting throughput tied strictly to stored size
Provisioned throughput at a fixed high level

explanation.correct: EFS Elastic throughput automatically scales performance up and down with demand and you pay for the throughput used, which suits spiky, unpredictable workloads.

distractors.A: Bursting throughput scales with stored data size and can throttle when credits are exhausted.
distractors.B: Fixed provisioned throughput pays for a set level even when idle, wasting money for spiky loads.
distractors.C: Instance store is not an EFS throughput mode.

explanation.exam_pattern: Spiky/unpredictable EFS demand with pay-for-use scaling = Elastic throughput.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (EFS throughput modes)

questions.stem: A database instance needs consistent EBS throughput that does not contend with the instance's regular network traffic. Which option BEST provides dedicated bandwidth between the instance and its EBS volumes?

options.text: Add more general network bandwidth only
Switch the volume to Cold HDD (sc1)

explanation.correct: EBS-optimized instances provide dedicated bandwidth to EBS, so storage I/O does not compete with other instance network traffic, giving more consistent EBS performance.

distractors.A: Transfer Acceleration applies to S3 uploads, not EBS I/O.
distractors.C: General bandwidth does not guarantee dedicated EBS throughput.
distractors.D: sc1 is a low-cost cold HDD; it lowers, not improves, performance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Consistent, dedicated EBS throughput = EBS-optimized instance.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (EBS-optimized)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Uploading a large object to Amazon S3 by splitting it into parts that transfer in parallel and can be retried individually is called a ___ upload. (one word, hyphen allowed)

explanation.correct: A multipart upload divides a large object into parts uploaded in parallel and reassembled by S3, improving speed and resilience.
explanation.exam_pattern: Large, parallel, resumable S3 upload = multipart upload.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable storage solutions (multipart upload)

questions.stem: A relational workload has intermittent, unpredictable bursts and is idle much of the time. The team wants database capacity to scale up and down automatically (even to a low level when idle) without choosing and managing fixed instance sizes. Which option BEST fits?

options.text: Self-managed MySQL on a large EC2 instance
A fixed-size provisioned Aurora instance sized for peak

explanation.correct: Aurora Serverless v2 automatically scales database capacity up and down in fine-grained steps to match load, which suits intermittent, unpredictable, or spiky relational workloads.

distractors.A: Self-managed MySQL on EC2 requires manual scaling and administration.
distractors.B: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store, not a relational engine for this relational workload.
distractors.D: A fixed peak-sized instance wastes money during idle periods and does not auto-scale.

explanation.exam_pattern: Auto-scaling relational capacity for spiky/intermittent load = Aurora Serverless v2.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (Aurora Serverless v2)

questions.stem: A new application will use DynamoDB but its traffic is completely unpredictable, with sudden spikes and quiet periods, and the team cannot forecast capacity. Which capacity mode BEST avoids throttling while requiring no capacity planning?

options.text: Adding a DAX cluster instead of choosing a capacity mode
Provisioned capacity with no auto scaling

explanation.correct: On-demand capacity automatically accommodates traffic up and down with no capacity planning and charges per request, ideal for unpredictable or spiky workloads.

distractors.A: DAX caches reads but does not replace the table's capacity mode for unpredictable write/read volume.
distractors.B: A fixed low capacity throttles during spikes.
distractors.C: Provisioned without auto scaling throttles when traffic exceeds the set capacity.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unpredictable DynamoDB traffic, no planning = on-demand capacity; steady/predictable = provisioned (+ auto scaling).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (DynamoDB on-demand)

questions.stem: A DynamoDB table is queried efficiently by its primary key, but a new feature must query items by a DIFFERENT, non-key attribute without scanning the whole table. Which feature BEST enables this?

options.text: Create a Global Secondary Index (GSI) on the needed attribute
Run a full table Scan for every query

explanation.correct: A Global Secondary Index lets you query on a different partition/sort key than the base table, giving efficient lookups on non-key attributes without scanning.

distractors.B: Larger items do not improve query access patterns.
distractors.C: Streams capture item-change events; they do not add a new query access pattern.
distractors.D: A full Scan reads the entire table and is slow and costly for targeted queries.

explanation.exam_pattern: Query DynamoDB by a non-key attribute = Global Secondary Index (GSI).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (DynamoDB GSI)

questions.stem: An Aurora cluster's read traffic varies widely. The team wants read queries automatically load-balanced across all Aurora Replicas, and the number of replicas to grow and shrink with load. Which combination BEST achieves this?

options.text: Send reads to the Aurora reader endpoint and enable Aurora Replica Auto Scaling
Point all reads at the cluster (writer) endpoint
Use a DynamoDB global table for the reads
Add a single manually managed replica

explanation.correct: The reader endpoint load-balances connections across available Aurora Replicas, and Replica Auto Scaling adds/removes replicas based on load, scaling reads automatically.

distractors.B: The writer/cluster endpoint targets the primary for writes; it does not load-balance reads across replicas.
distractors.C: DynamoDB is a different (NoSQL) service and does not serve an Aurora relational workload.
distractors.D: A single static replica does not scale with varying read demand.

explanation.exam_pattern: Auto-scaled, load-balanced Aurora reads = reader endpoint + Aurora Replica Auto Scaling.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (Aurora reader endpoint)

questions.stem: Many Lambda functions open and close their own connections to an RDS database, and during spikes the database runs out of available connections. Which solution BEST improves scalability by pooling and sharing connections?

options.text: Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database
A larger RDS instance class only

explanation.correct: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, so many short-lived Lambda invocations reuse a small set of connections, preventing connection exhaustion and improving scalability.

distractors.A: A read replica scales reads; it does not pool connections for the primary.
distractors.C: ElastiCache caches data but does not manage/pool the database's own connections.
distractors.D: A bigger instance raises the connection ceiling somewhat but still exhausts under many short-lived connections.

explanation.exam_pattern: Serverless/Lambda connection storms to RDS = RDS Proxy (connection pooling).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (RDS Proxy)

questions.stem: A business-intelligence team must run complex analytical queries with large aggregations and joins across petabytes of structured data in a columnar data warehouse. Which service BEST fits?

options.text: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL for OLTP

explanation.correct: Redshift is a columnar, massively parallel data warehouse optimized for complex analytical (OLAP) queries over very large datasets.

distractors.B: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not an analytics warehouse.
distractors.C: RDS/PostgreSQL is row-based and tuned for transactional (OLTP) workloads, not petabyte-scale analytics.
distractors.D: DynamoDB is a key-value/document store, not an analytical warehouse for complex joins/aggregations.

explanation.exam_pattern: Petabyte-scale analytical (OLAP) warehouse = Amazon Redshift; transactional = RDS/Aurora.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (Redshift)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Amazon RDS Proxy improves scalability by pooling and sharing database ___, which is especially helpful for serverless (Lambda) applications that open many short-lived sessions. (one word)

explanation.correct: RDS Proxy maintains a pool of database connections and shares them across application calls, reducing connection churn and exhaustion.
explanation.exam_pattern: RDS Proxy = pooled, shared database connections for serverless/high-concurrency apps.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing database solutions (RDS Proxy)

questions.stem: A company wants to run lightweight code at CloudFront edge locations to customize requests and responses (for example, header manipulation and simple authorization) close to users, minimizing latency. Which capability BEST provides this edge compute?

options.text: A single Lambda function in one Region behind the origin
Amazon API Gateway in one Region
Amazon EC2 in the origin Region

explanation.correct: Lambda@Edge and CloudFront Functions run code at edge locations to transform requests/responses and perform lightweight logic near users, reducing round trips to the origin.

distractors.A: A single-Region Lambda adds a round trip to that Region, increasing latency for distant users.
distractors.C: Regional API Gateway is not edge-local compute for CloudFront requests.
distractors.D: Origin-Region EC2 does not execute at the edge.

explanation.exam_pattern: Run code at the CDN edge near users = Lambda@Edge / CloudFront Functions.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (Lambda@Edge)

questions.stem: An application is deployed in several Regions. The team wants each user's DNS resolution to direct them to the Region that gives them the lowest network latency. Which Route 53 routing policy BEST achieves this?

explanation.correct: Latency-based routing directs each user to the Region that provides the lowest measured latency for them, improving response time across multi-Region deployments.

distractors.A: Weighted routing splits traffic by assigned proportions, not by latency.
distractors.C: Failover routing is for active-passive DR, not latency optimization.
distractors.D: Geolocation routes by the user's physical location (country/continent), not measured latency.

explanation.exam_pattern: Send users to the lowest-latency Region = Route 53 latency-based routing.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (Route 53 latency routing)

questions.stem: A company must return different endpoints (and localized content) to users based on the COUNTRY they are browsing from, for compliance and language reasons. Which Route 53 routing policy is designed for this?

explanation.correct: Geolocation routing answers DNS queries based on the user's geographic location (such as country), enabling localization and compliance-driven endpoint selection.

distractors.A: Latency routing optimizes for response time, not the user's country.
distractors.B: Simple routing returns a single record with no geographic logic.
distractors.D: Multivalue answer returns multiple healthy records for availability, not location-based selection.

explanation.exam_pattern: Route by user country/location = geolocation routing; by resource location + bias = geoproximity.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (Route 53 geolocation)

questions.stem: Two VPCs owned by the same company need low-latency private communication using private IP addresses, and only these two VPCs need to talk to each other. Which connection is the simplest, cost-effective choice?

options.text: Exposing services with public IPs and a load balancer
Routing the traffic over the public internet
A VPC peering connection between the two VPCs
A Site-to-Site VPN between the two VPCs

explanation.correct: VPC peering gives direct, private, low-latency connectivity between two VPCs using private IPs, and is simple and cost-effective for a single pair (note: peering is non-transitive).

distractors.A: Public IPs expose services unnecessarily and add internet-path latency.
distractors.B: The public internet adds latency and exposure versus private peering.
distractors.D: A VPN adds encryption overhead and is typically for hybrid/on-prem links, not simplest VPC-to-VPC.

explanation.exam_pattern: Private, low-latency link between two VPCs = VPC peering; many VPCs/transitive = Transit Gateway.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (VPC peering)

questions.stem: A CloudFront distribution serves content from an S3 origin. The team wants requests to automatically retry a secondary origin if the primary origin returns errors or is unreachable, improving reliability of delivery. Which CloudFront feature provides this?

options.text: A CloudFront origin group configured for origin failover
A single origin with a longer TTL
Route 53 simple routing to the bucket

explanation.correct: An origin group with primary and secondary origins enables CloudFront origin failover, automatically retrying the secondary origin on defined failure responses from the primary.

distractors.B: A longer TTL affects caching duration, not failover between origins.
distractors.C: Route 53 simple routing does not provide CDN origin-level failover within a distribution.
distractors.D: Disabling caching reduces performance and does not add origin failover.

explanation.exam_pattern: Automatic retry to a backup origin in CloudFront = origin group (origin failover).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (CloudFront origin failover)

questions.stem: An operations team wants to gradually shift user traffic between two Regional deployments by adjusting a bias value that expands or shrinks the geographic area served by each Region's resources. Which Route 53 routing policy supports this bias-based geographic control?

explanation.correct: Geoproximity routing routes based on the location of resources and lets you apply a bias to grow or shrink the region of users routed to a resource, shifting traffic between Regions.

distractors.A: Failover is active-passive DR, not gradual traffic shifting by geography.
distractors.B: Simple routing has no geographic or bias controls.
distractors.C: Geolocation routes strictly by the user's location without an adjustable bias to shift traffic.

explanation.exam_pattern: Shift traffic between Regions by adjustable geographic bias = geoproximity routing.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (Route 53 geoproximity)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: To send global users to the AWS Region that gives them the best response time, use Route 53 ___-based routing. (one word)

explanation.correct: Latency-based routing directs each user to the Region with the lowest latency for them.
explanation.exam_pattern: Lowest-latency Region selection = Route 53 latency-based routing.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 3 - Determine high-performing / scalable network architectures (Route 53 latency routing)

questions.stem: A workload runs on a modern Linux stack that can be recompiled for the ARM architecture. The team wants to lower compute cost while keeping or improving performance. Which change BEST achieves this?

options.text: Switch the workload to Dedicated Hosts
Run more copies of the same x86 instance

explanation.correct: Graviton (ARM) instances typically deliver better price-performance and lower cost than comparable x86 instances for workloads that can run on ARM.

distractors.A: Dedicated Hosts are a premium option for licensing/compliance, not cost reduction.
distractors.B: Adding x86 instances raises cost without the price-performance benefit of Graviton.
distractors.D: Larger x86 instances increase cost rather than improving price-performance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Lower compute cost with better price-performance on compatible workloads = AWS Graviton.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Graviton)

questions.stem: A steady production workload will stay on one specific EC2 instance family in a single Region for three years. The team wants the LARGEST committed-use discount and is willing to give up cross-family flexibility. Which purchase option BEST fits?

options.text: EC2 Instance Savings Plans (committed to that family/Region)

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Savings Plans give the deepest Savings Plan discount in exchange for committing to a specific instance family in a Region, while still allowing size flexibility within that family.

distractors.B: On-Demand has no commitment discount and is costliest for steady usage.
distractors.C: Spot can be interrupted and is unsuitable as the baseline for steady production capacity.
distractors.D: Compute Savings Plans are more flexible across families/Regions/Fargate/Lambda but give a smaller maximum discount.

explanation.exam_pattern: Max discount, locked to a family/Region = EC2 Instance Savings Plans; flexible across services = Compute Savings Plans.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Savings Plans types)

questions.stem: A scalable web fleet in an Auto Scaling group must keep a guaranteed baseline of always-available capacity but can run the elastic portion on cheaper, interruptible capacity to cut cost. Which approach BEST meets this?

options.text: An Auto Scaling mixed-instances policy combining On-Demand (baseline) with Spot (for the scalable portion)
All Spot instances for the entire fleet including the baseline

explanation.correct: A mixed-instances policy lets the group run a guaranteed On-Demand (or Reserved/Savings Plan) baseline and fill additional capacity with lower-cost Spot, balancing cost and availability.

distractors.B: All On-Demand misses the Spot savings for the elastic portion.
distractors.C: Running the baseline entirely on Spot risks interruptions to guaranteed capacity.
distractors.D: A single Reserved Instance does not provide elastic scaling or Spot savings.

explanation.exam_pattern: Guaranteed baseline + cheap elastic scale = ASG mixed-instances policy (On-Demand base + Spot).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (mixed instances + Spot)

questions.stem: A batch of stateless, fault-tolerant containers runs on AWS Fargate and can tolerate interruption. The team wants the lowest cost for this capacity. Which option BEST fits?

explanation.correct: Fargate Spot runs interruption-tolerant tasks on spare capacity at a significant discount, ideal for stateless, fault-tolerant batch containers.

distractors.A: Dedicated Hosts are a premium EC2 option, not a low-cost container choice.
distractors.C: Standard Fargate pricing is higher than Fargate Spot for interruptible work.
distractors.D: On-Demand EC2 misses the Spot discount and adds host management.

explanation.exam_pattern: Interruptible serverless containers at lowest cost = Fargate Spot.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Fargate Spot)

questions.stem: A lightly used internal service runs 24/7 on an EC2 instance but is only invoked occasionally during business hours, so most of the time the instance sits idle while still incurring cost. Which re-architecture MOST directly removes the idle cost?

options.text: Re-architect the service to AWS Lambda, paying only per invocation
Run the same idle instance on Spot
Purchase a 3-year Reserved Instance for the idle server
Move the service to a larger instance

explanation.correct: Moving occasional, event-driven work to Lambda eliminates charges during idle time because you pay only for actual executions.

distractors.B: Spot lowers price but still pays for an idle, always-on instance and risks interruption.
distractors.C: A Reserved Instance commits to paying for the idle server, locking in the waste.
distractors.D: A larger instance increases cost while the idle problem remains.

explanation.exam_pattern: Occasional/event-driven work wasting idle EC2 cost = re-architect to Lambda (pay-per-use).

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (serverless to remove idle cost)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: AWS's ARM-based processors, which often provide better price-performance and lower cost than comparable x86 instances, are called AWS ___. (one word)

explanation.correct: AWS Graviton processors are ARM-based and typically offer improved price-performance for compatible workloads.
explanation.exam_pattern: Lower-cost ARM instances with better price-performance = AWS Graviton.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized compute solutions (Graviton)

questions.stem: Before writing S3 Lifecycle rules, a team needs data showing which objects are accessed frequently versus rarely, to decide what to transition to Standard-IA. Which S3 feature provides this analysis?

explanation.correct: S3 Storage Class Analysis observes access patterns and recommends when to transition objects to infrequent-access storage, informing lifecycle policies.

distractors.A: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads; it does not analyze access patterns.
distractors.B: Requester Pays shifts cost to requesters; it does not analyze access for tiering.
distractors.C: Object Lock enforces WORM retention, not access analysis.

explanation.exam_pattern: Analyze access patterns to plan transitions = S3 Storage Class Analysis; auto-tier without analysis = Intelligent-Tiering.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized storage solutions (Storage Class Analysis)

questions.stem: A team must occasionally restore objects from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and wants the LOWEST retrieval cost when they can wait several hours for the data. Which retrieval option BEST fits?

explanation.correct: Bulk retrieval is the lowest-cost Glacier retrieval tier and is appropriate when a longer retrieval time (hours) is acceptable.

distractors.A: Standard retrieval is a middle option, costlier than Bulk.
distractors.B: Expedited retrieval is the fastest and most expensive option.
distractors.D: Provisioned capacity guarantees expedited retrieval throughput and adds cost, the opposite of cheapest.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cheapest Glacier retrieval when time-tolerant = Bulk; fastest/costliest = Expedited.

references: AWS SAA-C03 Exam Guide: Domain 4 - Design cost-optimized storage solutions (Glacier retrieval tiers)

questions.stem: An Amazon EFS file system holds many files that are rarely accessed after a while, and the team wants to cut storage cost automatically without changing the application. Which capability BEST achieves this?

options.text: Delete the file system each night
